items.content_text: Researchers have developed rBridge, a small proxy model with fewer than 1 billion parameters, that can predict the reasoning performance of much larger language models with over 100 times cost reduction. rBridge aligns closely with both the pre-training objective and the target reasoning tasks by weighting negative log-likelihood with task alignment and using reasoning traces from advanced models as reference. This approach enables effective dataset optimization before scaling up to large models, which typically require over 7 billion parameters to exhibit reliable reasoning capabilities. In experiments, rBridge demonstrated the strongest correlation with reasoning performance across six benchmarks for models ranging from 1 billion to 32 billion parameters. It also successfully transferred predictive relationships across different pre-training datasets in a zero-shot manner for models between 1 billion and 7 billion parameters. These results suggest that rBridge offers a practical and cost-efficient method for exploring reasoning-oriented pre-training in large language models.

items.title: Researchers propose K-Merge, a data-free, efficient method for online continual merging of Low-Rank Adapters on-device to support multiple tasks under storage constraints [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced K-Merge, a novel method designed for on-device deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) that efficiently merges Low-Rank Adapters (LoRAs) to support multiple tasks within limited storage constraints. This approach addresses the challenge of incrementally incorporating new LoRAs as users request support for additional tasks, ensuring that performance on previously supported tasks is maintained without requiring access to original training data. K-Merge operates in a data-free and computationally efficient manner, selecting and merging adapters when new ones become available, while respecting the storage and computational limits typical of mobile devices. Extensive experiments on real-world tasks demonstrate that K-Merge outperforms existing strategies, making it a promising solution for continual learning and adaptation of LLMs on resource-constrained devices.

items.title: Researchers propose FlowPath, an invertible neural flow method that learns data-driven manifolds for improved classification of irregularly-sampled time series, showing significant accuracy gains on 18 benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced FlowPath, a novel method that uses invertible neural flows to learn data-driven manifolds for classifying irregularly-sampled time series. This approach improves upon traditional fixed interpolation methods by constructing continuous, data-adaptive control paths that better represent the underlying data geometry, leading to enhanced classification accuracy. FlowPath enforces invertibility constraints to ensure information preservation and well-behaved transformations, distinguishing it from previous models that lacked such constraints. Evaluations on 18 benchmark datasets and a real-world case study demonstrate that FlowPath consistently outperforms baseline methods, highlighting the importance of modeling both the dynamics and geometry of control paths in irregular time series analysis. These findings suggest that incorporating learned geometric structures into time series models can provide more robust and generalizable solutions, especially in scenarios with sparse or irregular data sampling. FlowPath offers a promising direction for advancing continuous-time dynamics modeling in machine learning.

items.title: Researchers find 8-bit quantization improves continual learning retention and efficiency in large language models compared to FP16, with INT8 balancing plasticity and knowledge retention [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that 8-bit quantization improves continual learning retention and efficiency in large language models compared to the commonly used FP16 precision. Their study reveals that while FP16 models perform better initially, quantized models, especially those using INT8 and INT4 precision, outperform FP16 on subsequent tasks by 8-15%, with INT4 nearly doubling FP16's performance in code generation. The research highlights that even minimal replay buffers significantly enhance knowledge retention, with INT8 striking the best balance between learning adaptability and memory retention. The team suggests that the noise introduced by quantization acts as a form of implicit regularization, reducing overfitting to new tasks that often affects higher-precision models. Their findings challenge the assumption that higher precision always yields better results, proposing that INT8 quantization offers both computational efficiency and improved continual learning dynamics. Practical guidelines from the study recommend small replay buffers for natural language understanding tasks and moderate buffers for math and code tasks, with quantized models requiring less replay to maintain performance comparable to FP16.

items.title: Researchers use AlphaEarth satellite-derived embeddings to improve hydrological model accuracy in predicting river flow in ungauged basins by capturing complex environmental patterns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated that AlphaEarth Foundation embeddings, derived from extensive satellite imagery, can improve the accuracy of hydrological models in predicting river flow in ungauged basins. These embeddings capture complex environmental patterns such as vegetation, land surface properties, and long-term dynamics more effectively than traditional basin attributes, leading to better performance in flow predictions for basins not included in training data. The study also highlights the importance of selecting donor basins with similar environmental and hydrological characteristics based on these embeddings to enhance prediction accuracy. Incorporating many dissimilar basins was found to reduce model performance. These findings suggest that satellite-informed environmental representations can strengthen hydrological forecasting and facilitate the development of adaptable models for diverse landscapes.

items.title: Researchers introduce KAGE-Bench, a fast JAX-native benchmark isolating visual generalization failures in pixel-based reinforcement learning with 34 train-evaluation pairs and up to 33M steps per second [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed KAGE-Bench, a JAX-native benchmark designed to isolate and evaluate visual generalization failures in pixel-based reinforcement learning agents. The benchmark is built on KAGE-Env, a 2D platformer environment that separates visual factors into independently controllable axes while maintaining consistent underlying control tasks. KAGE-Bench includes 34 train-evaluation pairs across six visual shift categories, enabling precise analysis of how different visual changes impact agent performance. Using a standard PPO-CNN baseline, the study found that certain visual shifts, such as changes in background and lighting, significantly impair agent success, whereas alterations in agent appearance have less effect. Some visual changes allowed agents to maintain forward movement but prevented task completion, indicating that reward metrics alone may not fully capture generalization issues. The fully vectorized JAX implementation supports up to 33 million environment steps per second on a single GPU, facilitating rapid and reproducible testing across visual variations.

items.title: PaAno proposes lightweight patch-based representation learning for time-series anomaly detection, achieving state-of-the-art results on TSB-AD benchmark with faster, more efficient inference than transformer-based models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced PaAno, a lightweight patch-based representation learning method for time-series anomaly detection that achieves state-of-the-art results on the TSB-AD benchmark. Unlike recent approaches relying on large neural networks such as transformers, PaAno uses a 1D convolutional neural network to embed short temporal patches from training data, enabling faster and more efficient inference suitable for real-time and resource-constrained environments. PaAno is trained with a combination of triplet loss and pretext loss to capture meaningful temporal patterns in the data. During inference, it computes anomaly scores by comparing embeddings of patches around each time step to those of normal patches from training data. Evaluations show that PaAno significantly outperforms existing methods, including heavy architectures, on both univariate and multivariate time-series anomaly detection across various performance metrics.

items.title: Researchers propose calibrated test-time guidance methods for Bayesian inference, correcting posterior sampling errors and improving black hole image reconstruction PSNR [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified that common test-time guidance methods used in pretrained diffusion models do not accurately sample from the true Bayesian posterior, resulting in miscalibrated inference. They analyzed the structural approximations causing this issue and proposed new estimators that enable calibrated sampling from the Bayesian posterior, improving the accuracy of Bayesian inference. Their approach significantly outperforms existing methods across various Bayesian inference tasks and achieves a new state-of-the-art peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) in black hole image reconstruction, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing image quality in this complex application.

items.title: Researchers develop competition-aware CPC forecasting model using 1.66 billion Google Ads records for car rental market, improving accuracy up to 27.6% over 12 weeks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a competition-aware forecasting model for cost-per-click (CPC) in paid search advertising, using 1.66 billion Google Ads records from the car rental market between 2021 and 2023. The model integrates semantic keyword relationships, behavioral patterns from CPC trajectories, and geographic market data to improve prediction accuracy. It outperforms traditional statistical and machine learning baselines, achieving up to a 27.6% reduction in forecasting error over a 12-week horizon, particularly for high-CPC, high-volatility keywords where accurate predictions are most critical. The study constructs a weekly panel of 1,811 keyword series over 127 weeks and employs spatiotemporal graph forecasting techniques that incorporate competition-aware proxies derived from keyword text, CPC trends, and localized demand. The model's effectiveness is supported by tests showing that its gains are specific to competitive dynamics rather than generic smoothing effects. These findings highlight the importance of considering competitive interactions in auction-driven advertising markets under partial observability and suggest a horizon-dependent approach to CPC forecasting.

items.title: Researchers propose DeLL framework using dynamic knowledge spaces and causal inference to improve lifelong learning and adaptability in end-to-end autonomous driving systems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed DeLL, a Deconfounded Lifelong Learning framework designed to enhance end-to-end autonomous driving systems by addressing challenges such as catastrophic forgetting, knowledge transfer difficulties, and spurious correlations caused by unobservable confounders. DeLL integrates a Dirichlet process mixture model to create dynamic knowledge spaces for clustering driving behaviors and discovering latent abilities, combined with a causal inference technique called front-door adjustment to mitigate misleading correlations and improve learned representations. The framework allows adaptive knowledge expansion without predefined cluster numbers, reducing forgetting and improving adaptability to new driving scenarios. An evolutionary trajectory decoder supports non-autoregressive planning, and new evaluation protocols based on Bench2Drive assess lifelong learning performance. Tests in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that DeLL significantly boosts driving performance and knowledge retention in autonomous driving systems.

items.title: Researchers propose Mutual Information Preference Optimization to improve LLM performance by 3-51% without additional data using contrastive data augmentation and direct preference optimization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Mutual Information Preference Optimization (MIPO), a novel method to enhance large language model (LLM) performance by maximizing mutual information between prompts and responses without requiring additional data. MIPO uses contrastive data augmentation to create preference pairs, generating positive responses based on correct prompts and negative responses from unrelated prompts, and applies Direct Preference Optimization to learn from these pairs. Experiments with Llama and Qwen instruct models demonstrate performance improvements ranging from 3% to 51%, including gains in both personalized and verifiable tasks such as math and multiple-choice question answering. This approach addresses limitations of current post-training methods that depend heavily on costly human-labeled data or external verification, offering a self-improvement framework that leverages intrinsic signals within the model. The results suggest that MIPO can effectively boost LLM capabilities across diverse domains without external supervision, pointing to a promising direction for future research in model optimization and autonomous learning.

items.title: Researchers present Crystalite, a lightweight diffusion Transformer with Subatomic Tokenization and Geometry Enhancement Module for efficient crystal modeling, achieving state-of-the-art prediction and faster sampling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Crystalite, a lightweight diffusion Transformer designed for efficient crystal modeling. This model introduces two key innovations: Subatomic Tokenization, which offers a compact and chemically structured atom representation, and the Geometry Enhancement Module (GEM), which incorporates periodic geometric information directly into the attention mechanism. These features enable Crystalite to maintain the simplicity and efficiency of standard Transformers while better capturing the structure of crystalline materials. Crystalite achieves state-of-the-art performance on crystal structure prediction benchmarks and excels in de novo crystal generation, attaining the highest S.U.N. discovery score among evaluated methods. Additionally, it samples significantly faster than existing geometry-intensive models, offering a more efficient approach to generative modeling of crystalline materials.

items.title: Researchers introduce GUI-Perturbed framework revealing systematic accuracy drops in GUI grounding models on spatial reasoning tasks and visual perturbations, releasing dataset and fine-tuned model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed GUI-Perturbed, a framework that reveals significant accuracy declines in GUI grounding models when handling spatial reasoning tasks and visual perturbations. While these models typically achieve over 85% accuracy on standard benchmarks, their performance drops by 27 to 56 percentage points with relational instructions requiring spatial understanding. The framework independently varies visual scenes and instructions to assess robustness, uncovering systematic accuracy collapses across three evaluated 7B models and notable degradation under visual changes like browser zoom. The study highlights that current benchmarks, which test each screenshot with a single fixed instruction, fail to detect these weaknesses. Additionally, attempts to improve performance through rank-8 LoRA fine-tuning with augmented data unexpectedly reduced accuracy. By isolating specific capability axes such as spatial reasoning and visual robustness, GUI-Perturbed provides diagnostic insights beyond aggregate benchmarks. The researchers have released the dataset, augmentation pipeline, and a fine-tuned model to support further investigation and development in this area.

items.title: Researchers propose Fed-FSTQ, a Fisher-guided token quantization method that reduces uplink traffic by 46x and speeds federated fine-tuning of large language models on edge devices by 52% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Fed-FSTQ, a Fisher-guided token quantization method designed to enhance communication efficiency in federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) on edge devices. This approach significantly reduces uplink traffic by 46 times and accelerates training speed by 52%, addressing challenges posed by heterogeneous bandwidth and intermittent device participation in mobile environments. Fed-FSTQ uses a lightweight Fisher information proxy to assess token importance, enabling selective token transmission with mixed-precision quantization that prioritizes critical information while minimizing redundant data. The method integrates seamlessly with existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning frameworks like LoRA without altering server aggregation and supports clients with varying bandwidth through compact sparse message packing. Experiments on multilingual and medical question-answering tasks under non-independent and identically distributed data conditions demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing communication overhead and improving training efficiency. Additionally, applying Fisher-guided token reduction during inference yields up to a 1.55-fold speedup on resource-constrained edge devices such as NVIDIA Jetson, highlighting Fed-FSTQ's practical deployability in real-world scenarios with limited computational resources.

items.title: Korzhinskii-Net physics-informed neural network models subsurface mineral prospectivity across six ore provinces, outperforming classical baselines with open-source pipeline [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Korzhinskii-Net is a physics-informed neural network designed to improve subsurface mineral prospectivity modeling by integrating physical processes such as Darcy flow, heat transport, and reaction rates into a differentiable forward model. Tested across six ore provinces with different commodity types, it significantly outperforms traditional data-driven classifiers, achieving a mean PR-AUC of 0.708 compared to 0.235 for the best classical baseline. This approach leverages surface and remote-sensing data while capturing subsurface physics that conventional models often overlook. The model is named after Dmitri S. Korzhinskii, whose theory of infiltration metasomatism underpins the physical framework. Evaluations used a rigorous cross-validation protocol with controlled data leakage and disabled baseline proxy features, confirming consistent improvements across diverse geological settings. The full pipeline and evaluation tools have been released as open source, enabling further research and application in mineral exploration.

items.title: Researchers introduce Topological Neural Dynamics, a neuron-wise sequence modeling framework that outperforms RNN, LSTM, and Transformer baselines in behavior cloning tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Topological Neural Dynamics (TND), a novel sequence modeling framework that shifts from traditional layer-wise dynamics to neuron-wise dynamics, allowing each neuron to evolve independently within a directed graph structure. This approach contrasts with existing models like RNNs, LSTMs, and Transformers, which use shared operators for all neurons in a layer. TND was tested on a behavior cloning task in single-player Pong, where it significantly outperformed baseline models, achieving over three times the consecutive catch rate of the strongest competitor. TND models neural systems as discrete-time graph-coupled dynamical systems, where collective computation emerges from interactions defined by explicit graph topology. The framework's neuron-wise dynamics provide a more flexible and effective inductive bias for sequence modeling, suggesting potential improvements in modeling complex dynamical systems by capturing local neuron interactions rather than enforcing uniform layer-wise evolution.

items.title: Study finds safety guardrails in eight large language models fail up to 100% for several mental health conditions, raising concerns over their use in public settings [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A recent study evaluated eight proprietary large language models (LLMs) for their safety in handling mental health-related conversations across 16 DSM-5 conditions. The research found that while safeguards were generally effective for suicide and self-harm, they failed completely for several other conditions, including eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder, with failure rates reaching up to 100%. This raises significant concerns about the reliability of these models in sensitive public settings such as schools, search engines, and consumer chatbots. The study introduced a comprehensive harm taxonomy and a multi-dimensional evaluation framework to assess the models under various adversarial attacks. The findings highlight the inconsistency and inadequacy of current safety measures, emphasizing the need for clearly defined harm categories and robust safeguards tailored to different clinical conditions. Until such improvements are implemented, the use of these LLMs in public-facing applications poses considerable risks to vulnerable populations.

items.title: Researchers propose a certification-inspired dual-gate pipeline to reduce word error rate by up to 55% and enhance robustness in automatic speech recognition systems across four architectures [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a certification-inspired dual-gate pipeline to improve the robustness of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems, achieving up to a 55% reduction in Word Error Rate (WER) across four different architectures. This approach addresses the challenge of detecting errors in deployed ASR systems without access to true transcriptions by using a Two-Sided Atomic Audit to certify token existence and adversarial exclusion, combined with a Rank-Based Tournament to select the best transcription sequence. The method enhances acoustic security by providing detailed word- and sentence-level certifications, increasing recall, and reducing the correlation between confidence scores and errors. This advancement offers a promising direction for making ASR systems more reliable against both adversarial and benign perturbations in real-world applications.

items.title: Researchers simulate over 8 million over-the-air acoustic attacks, revealing up to 94.5% word error rate increases and introducing a Dual-Form Signal to Noise Ratio to separate source stealth from attack efficacy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have conducted over 8 million simulations of over-the-air acoustic attacks on voice-controlled AI systems, revealing that such attacks can increase word error rates by up to 94.5% in models like Whisper and wav2vec. They introduced a novel Dual-Form Signal to Noise Ratio metric to distinguish between the stealthiness of the attack source and the effectiveness of the attack itself, addressing a key limitation in previous studies. The study highlights the challenges of translating digital adversarial attacks into the physical acoustic environment, which has often been oversimplified in prior research. By using a high-throughput simulation framework combined with real-world testing, the researchers provide a more accurate understanding of the risks posed by acoustic attacks and establish a foundation for reproducible and verifiable research that fully incorporates acoustic factors.

items.title: Researchers propose Training-Free Gated Reranking to reduce computational costs by up to 80% and improve few-shot learning performance by up to 2% across 8 LLMs and multiple datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Training-Free Gated Reranking, a method that selectively applies reranking to few-shot learning examples based on model uncertainty. This approach challenges the common assumption that reranking always enhances performance, showing that it can sometimes degrade results. Experiments involving eight large language models across multiple natural language understanding and machine translation datasets demonstrate that this method reduces computational costs by 15% to 80% while improving average performance by up to 2%. The study highlights that higher computational expense does not necessarily lead to better outcomes and that reranking is most effective when focused on instances where the model exhibits high uncertainty. This targeted strategy offers a more efficient use of resources in few-shot learning scenarios without sacrificing, and often improving, model accuracy.

items.title: Researchers introduce FinPersona-Bench to measure mandate salience decay in autonomous financial agents using 18 LLMs with varying behavioral profiles in simulated market scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed FinPersona-Bench, a simulation benchmark designed to measure Mandate Salience Decay (MSD) in autonomous financial agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). MSD refers to the gradual loss of influence of explicit behavioral mandates, such as capital preservation or avoiding speculative bets, as market context accumulates over time. The benchmark evaluates 18 LLMs with varying behavioral profiles in synthetic market scenarios that separate observable prices from hidden fundamental values, testing for failures like trading without signals, panic-selling during crashes, and ignoring fundamentals during bubbles. The study found that MSD increases over time and varies by model, with significant behavioral differences emerging between agents that receive periodic mandate re-grounding and those that do not, especially during market crashes. While re-grounding mandates benefits conservative agents in low-signal markets, it can worsen performance for aggressive agents under the same conditions. These results highlight the need for selective, mandate-aware re-grounding strategies tailored to agent profiles and market environments to ensure reliable long-term deployment of autonomous financial agents.

items.title: Researchers introduce Constructive Alignment paradigm to govern evolving human preference dynamics in human-AI interaction using a control-theoretic framework [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose a new paradigm called Constructive Alignment to address the dynamic nature of human preferences in human-AI interactions. Unlike traditional AI alignment approaches that treat preferences as fixed targets, this framework views preferences as evolving and shaped through ongoing interaction with adaptive AI systems. Using a control-theoretic model, the approach focuses on guiding the development of human values over time rather than merely satisfying static preferences. The Constructive Alignment paradigm draws on insights from behavioral economics, psychology, and social theory to model preferences as layered states influenced by AI actions and interaction design. It emphasizes regulating how AI systems affect human evaluative states to ensure that evolving preferences remain coherent, reflectively endorsed, epistemically grounded, resistant to manipulation, and empowering under uncertainty. This shift reframes alignment as governing long-term value formation in human-AI relationships.

items.title: Researchers propose Bounded Morality framework to analyze computational limits of moral reasoning in finite agents, defining tradeoffs between moral breadth and depth for AI alignment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced the Bounded Morality framework to analyze the computational challenges of moral reasoning in finite agents. This framework extends the concept of bounded rationality by defining moral situations along two dimensions: moral breadth, which covers the range of entities considered morally relevant, and moral depth, which involves the complexity of evaluating their interactions. The study highlights an inherent tradeoff between these dimensions due to limited computational resources, framing ethical theories as strategies optimized for different conditions rather than absolute moral truths. The framework also introduces formal concepts of moral regret and moral progress within these constraints, suggesting that effective moral alignment in artificial intelligence depends more on how moral reasoning capacity is scaled and allocated than on simply mimicking human moral judgments. This approach offers a new perspective on designing AI systems capable of nuanced ethical decision-making under resource limitations.

items.title: Researchers present MMM data model for knowledge interoperability in decentralizable knowledge commons, combining normative constraints with free-text labels and demonstrating early usability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced MMM, a new data model designed to improve knowledge interoperability within decentralizable knowledge commons. MMM addresses limitations of traditional document-centric systems by combining a small set of normative constraints with the flexibility of free-text labels, enabling interdisciplinary collaboration without requiring strict semantic alignment. The model aims to balance formal structure with human usability, supporting knowledge documentation across various disciplines and applications. The development of MMM stems from practical needs in interdisciplinary research and is positioned within a broader analysis of information system design. A reference implementation and pilot deployment demonstrate its feasibility and early usability, suggesting potential for wider adoption in environments where knowledge sharing and reuse are critical but challenging under existing document-based frameworks.

items.title: Researchers propose a constrained, verifiable agent framework using typed JSON configurations for reliable open-web data collection, validated on 138 tasks with low execution time and reusable execution paths [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a constrained, verifiable agent framework to improve the reliability of web data collection by large language models (LLMs). Instead of generating free-form code, the framework uses typed JSON configurations based on a six-type collector taxonomy, combined with template constraints, static execution, and rule-based quality checks. This approach addresses common issues like dependency errors and schema mismatches in web scraping. The framework was tested on 138 tasks, demonstrating that stable data collection requires detailed constraints beyond initial descriptions. On 80 independently verified tasks, it achieved zero execution-stage LLM token usage and the lowest average execution time, offering a reusable and deterministic process suited for repeated scheduled data collection. These results suggest the framework provides a low-cost, verifiable solution for reliable open-web data gathering.

items.title: Researchers develop conflict-free solution-space path-planning algorithm for en-route air traffic control with interpretable displays and efficient conflict detection, tested on Maastricht Upper Area Control Centre scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a conflict-free path-planning algorithm designed to support en-route air traffic control by aligning with air traffic controllers' operational needs. The algorithm emphasizes interpretability and flexibility through solution-space displays, allowing controllers to see all feasible safe actions and adapt to changing optimization goals. It integrates three intent-based conflict detection methods-distance-based, time-interval-based, and zone-based-within a computationally efficient framework to identify safe paths. Two variants of the solution space path planning algorithm, based on vertex and edge search nodes, were evaluated for speed and solution quality. Testing on scenarios from the Maastricht Upper Area Control Centre's Delta sector showed that the vertex-based variant combined with zone-based conflict detection performed best, computing conflict-free paths in an average of 3.69 milliseconds using a 5 nautical mile grid. This approach aims to enhance decision support for tactical air traffic controllers by providing interpretable, efficient, and practical routing solutions.

items.title: Researchers introduce RareDxR1, a large language model for autonomous rare disease diagnosis from unstructured clinical notes, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy without human annotation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed RareDxR1, a large language model designed to autonomously diagnose rare diseases directly from unstructured clinical notes. This model addresses limitations of previous AI methods by internalizing fragmented rare disease knowledge and employing a novel training framework that combines knowledge internalization with autonomous evolutionary learning, eliminating the need for structured phenotypes or human annotation. RareDxR1 also introduces Reflection-Enhanced Reasoning Sampling to mimic expert diagnostic reasoning and uses a dual-level curriculum reinforcement learning approach to improve diagnostic accuracy. Experimental results show that RareDxR1 achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, representing a significant advancement in open-domain rare disease diagnosis. The researchers plan to make their code and dataset publicly available, potentially facilitating further research and development in this critical area of medical AI.

items.title: Researchers introduce a contextual-bandit oversight game modeling two-sided informational asymmetry between human supervisors and AI agents, analyzing oversight gaps and dynamic resolution mechanisms [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a contextual-bandit oversight game to model the two-sided informational asymmetry between human supervisors and AI agents. In this framework, humans privately know their reward functions while AI agents have private knowledge about the quality of their proposed actions, reflecting real-world scenarios where AI assesses situations beyond human direct observation. The study builds on Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning and the Oversight Game, introducing a play/ask/trust/oversee interface that allows precise one-shot characterizations of oversight dynamics without the complexity of full state transitions. The analysis identifies a gap between an optimal team strategy and a myopic human oversight rule, revealing a zone where AI knows an action is harmful and shutdown would be beneficial, yet the human supervisor, relying on prior beliefs, opts not to intervene. This oversight gap arises from non-credible communication between AI and humans. The researchers also explore how this gap can diminish over repeated interactions through passive learning and active signaling, despite a delay in oversight responses, offering insights into improving human-AI collaboration and safety in autonomous systems.

items.title: Study introduces Epistemic AI Literacy framework to analyze student-GenAI co-programming interactions, finding 78.8% rely on non-mastery aims and unreliable epistemic strategies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A new study introduces the Epistemic AI Literacy (EAIL) framework to analyze how students interact with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) during co-programming tasks. The research examines students' epistemic aims and processes, such as query construction, output evaluation, and problem-solving regulation, revealing that 78.8% of interactions rely on non-mastery-oriented aims and less reliable strategies like outsourcing and verification-seeking. Only 11.1% of interactions demonstrated high epistemic engagement, combining mastery-oriented aims with advanced strategies like epistemic justification. Using a large dataset of human-AI co-programming dialogues, the study operationalizes dimensions of epistemic aims and processes based on the AIR framework, highlighting the dynamic nature of AI literacy as an epistemic phenomenon emerging through human-AI interaction. The findings suggest a widespread lack of effective epistemic engagement among students when working with GenAI, underscoring the need for educational approaches that foster more reliable and mastery-focused epistemic strategies in AI-supported learning environments.

items.title: Researchers find memory architecture influences language emergence in LLM agents more than channel capacity, with persistent notebooks improving coordination in signaling games [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers investigated how two agents develop a shared language from scratch using Lewis signaling games, focusing on the impact of memory architecture versus channel capacity in large language model (LLM) agents. Their study of five memory architectures revealed that memory design plays a more critical role than channel capacity in achieving reliable coordination. Agents equipped with a persistent private notebook, which externalizes learned conventions, outperformed stateless agents by maintaining stable communication even as vocabulary size increased, reaching a coordination reliability of approximately 0.867 at higher channel capacities. The study found that stateless agents performed best at moderate channel capacities but deteriorated as the vocabulary expanded beyond what their limited context windows could handle. Contrary to predictions based on information bottleneck theory, which suggested an optimal channel capacity matching the number of objects, the researchers observed that this bottleneck point was a vulnerability, and having surplus capacity generally improved performance. Their findings emphasize that both memory architecture and channel capacity must be considered together to understand how stable communication systems and languages emerge from interaction history.

items.title: Researchers present Seed2.0 model series addressing long-tail knowledge and complex instruction following to improve real-world task performance and reasoning capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Seed2.0, a new model series designed to tackle complex real-world tasks by focusing on users' genuine needs and developing a robust evaluation system based on realistic scenarios. The model addresses key challenges such as long-tail knowledge and complex instruction following, significantly enhancing its reliability on intricate, long-duration tasks. Seed2.0 also offers advanced reasoning, visual understanding, and search capabilities that meet the common requirements of a wide user base. The development of Seed2.0 involved selecting and abstracting benchmarks that reflect real user demands, guiding the model's improvements. Extensive real-world use cases demonstrate that Seed2.0 is beginning to effectively manage complex tasks, providing increased value to hundreds of millions of users. This advancement marks a meaningful step toward improving AI performance in practical, multifaceted environments.

items.title: Researchers introduce Mnemosyne, an open-source runtime implementing Agentic Transaction Processing to validate and repair AI-generated workflows with safety guarantees and under 6% overhead [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Mnemosyne, an open-source runtime that implements Agentic Transaction Processing (ATP) to validate and repair AI-generated workflows with safety guarantees and minimal overhead. ATP treats AI-generated actions as untrusted proposals that must pass deterministic checks against a defined constraint set before being committed, ensuring correctness regardless of the proposing agent's reliability. Mnemosyne features an append-only transition log, state projection, dependency-safe compensation, and active commitment records, and it enforces four key safety properties along with a bounded reactive repair protocol. The system was tested against nine falsification scenarios, successfully rejecting invalid actions while admitting valid ones, with less than 6% overhead for projection and validation. Its localized repair protocol significantly reduces the number of operations needed for corrections compared to global recomputation. Mnemosyne is available as an open-source project, providing a practical tool for enhancing the reliability and safety of AI-generated workflows.

items.title: Researchers develop gear-based managed autonomy system for single- and multi-agent cyber-physical systems, achieving 99.6% anomaly detection and formal safety certification in robotic assembly tests [ ~ ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a gear-based managed autonomy system called \system{} that enhances safety and governance for both single- and multi-agent cyber-physical systems. This discrete-time control system integrates five execution gears with utility-gated dispatch and event-driven fallback to address common failure modes such as safety violations, behavioral instability, and error state continuity loss. The system demonstrates monotonic stability and execution safety for single agents and provides distributed safety guarantees, including zero collisions, for multi-agent setups. The approach applies the \smart{} managed-autonomy lifecycle to map runtime evidence into governance states and uses consensus gating, swarm-level analysis, and per-agent gear authority to maintain stability. Evaluated on a three-agent UR5 robotic assembly cell with fault data from the NIST robot arm accuracy dataset, the system achieved a 99.6% anomaly detection rate, significantly outperforming the single-agent baseline, and reduced detection latency by 3.5 times. It also provides a formal safety certificate for the physical workspace, separating action control from autonomy governance through its execution gears.

items.title: Researchers propose SPIRE framework to learn latent design intents for personalized slide generation via structural denoising and multi-agent reinforcement learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced SPIRE, a new framework designed to improve personalized slide generation by learning latent design intents through structural denoising and multi-agent reinforcement learning. This approach addresses the limitations of current AI methods that rely heavily on predefined templates or detailed user instructions, which often fail to capture fine-grained, page-level design preferences. SPIRE formulates slide personalization as an inverse planning problem and enables two agents to collaboratively refine slide designs without requiring knowledge of the specific tools used to create them.

items.title: Researchers introduce PHREEQC-MCQ-200 benchmark with 200 questions to evaluate tool-augmented AI agents on aqueous-geochemistry simulations, revealing accuracy gains and regressions across model types [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed PHREEQC-MCQ-200, a benchmark consisting of 200 multiple-choice questions designed to evaluate AI agents augmented with scientific tools on aqueous-geochemistry simulations. The benchmark tests agents' abilities to create simulator inputs, run the PHREEQC software, analyze outputs, and provide accurate answers. Results show that access to the simulator generally improves accuracy across various AI models, but also reveals cases where tool use causes performance regressions that average accuracy metrics can obscure. The study highlights the importance of how AI agents access and interpret simulator outputs, noting that interfaces like a table-of-contents can reduce computational costs and enhance accuracy for advanced models, while hindering mid-tier models that struggle with structured data. The researchers emphasize that evaluating scientific AI agents should go beyond overall accuracy to include detailed diagnostics such as item-level retention, sensitivity to output access methods, and points of failure in the computational process.

items.title: Researchers present Agri-SAGE, a simulation-grounded multi-agent LLM framework integrating APSIM biophysical simulation for context-aware agricultural advisory generation, outperforming static guidelines in a 10-year retrospective study [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Agri-SAGE, a novel framework that combines multi-agent large language models (LLMs) with APSIM biophysical simulation to generate context-aware agricultural advisories. This approach addresses the limitations of static agronomic guidelines, which lack responsiveness to in-season variability, and previous LLM-based systems that may produce recommendations lacking physiological validity. Agri-SAGE integrates retrieval-grounded reasoning with simulation to both generate and validate agronomic advice, improving decision-making in agriculture. The framework was evaluated using three reasoning methods-Plan-and-Solve, Tree of Thoughts, and Reflexion-over a retrospective 10-year analysis. All methods outperformed traditional static Package-of-Practice baselines, with Tree of Thoughts achieving the highest peak yields. Reflexion offered similar agronomic results while reducing computational costs by utilizing cross-seasonal episodic memory, demonstrating efficient and effective advisory generation.

items.title: Researchers present MuSix, a multi-scale mixture of world models framework for embodied agents that improves reasoning and adaptation in evolving environments, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MuSix, a multi-scale mixture of world models framework designed for embodied agents operating in dynamic real-world environments. MuSix addresses challenges in multi-scale reasoning and knowledge adaptation by introducing a scale-aware routing mechanism and scale-dependent update policies, enabling agents to better handle situational novelty and varying rates of knowledge obsolescence. This approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in experiments on benchmarks such as EmbodiedBench and HAZARD. MuSix employs a two-stage routing process inspired by Construal Level Theory, where a meta-router assigns weights over a continuous scale space based on experiential distance, followed by base routers selecting appropriate world models within the chosen scale. The framework also incorporates scale-dependent forgetting rates to allow rapid updating of low-scale knowledge while preserving high-scale abstractions, with gated inter-scale transfer ensuring coherence across the hierarchy.

items.title: Researchers define AI-native games by runtime generative AI as core gameplay, analyze 53 examples, and propose a taxonomy and roadmap for design, evaluation, and safety [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have defined AI-native games as those in which runtime generative AI is essential to the core gameplay loop, meaning that removing or replacing the AI would fundamentally alter the game's play. They analyzed 53 publicly available AI-native games and prototypes, distinguishing these from AI-augmented games and other AI-assisted content by this criterion. The study introduces a dual-axis taxonomy categorizing games by player-facing type and the dominant AI mechanic that makes generative AI indispensable. The analysis found that most AI-native games focus on language-driven designs such as narrative adventures and generative storytelling, while other categories like multi-agent simulation and generative construction are less common. The researchers emphasize that a key design challenge is maintaining stable gameplay despite the semantic openness of AI-generated content, relying on consistent goals, rules, and player agency. They conclude with a roadmap addressing controllable generation, AI mechanics, multimodal systems, evaluation, safety, and regulation in AI-native game design.

items.title: Researchers introduce HARC, a fine-tuning method coupling harmfulness and refusal directions in LLMs to improve safety alignment and robustness across multiple model families and scales [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed HARC, a fine-tuning method designed to enhance the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) by coupling harmfulness and refusal directions within the models. This approach addresses vulnerabilities that allow jailbreaks by targeting the internal representations of harmful content and refusal signals at both prompt and response token positions. HARC confines its intervention to the harmfulness-refusal subspace, preserving the model's overall capabilities while improving robustness against safety breaches. The study reveals that jailbreak attacks manipulate either the refusal or harmfulness directions before token generation, with different attack types occupying distinct regions in this subspace. Notably, models can recognize harmful content during generation even if they fail to detect it at the prompt stage. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HARC outperforms six baseline safety methods across multiple model families and scales without requiring architecture-specific adjustments, achieving a strong balance between robustness, capability, and usability.

items.title: Researchers introduce AGI Maze, a lightweight benchmark framework for testing world-modeling capabilities of language model agents in partially observable, stateful environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed AGI Maze, a lightweight benchmark framework designed to test the world-modeling capabilities of language model agents in environments that are partially observable and stateful. Unlike traditional large language models (LLMs) that predict the next token based on static context, AGI Maze challenges agents to build and use persistent representations of the environment through grid-based maze tasks with varying difficulty levels. Initial tests show that standard LLMs struggle to internally represent these mazes during inference, highlighting limitations in their reasoning abilities in dynamic settings. The framework avoids high-dimensional sensory inputs and focuses on requiring agents to maintain memory and form structured hypotheses about hidden states. A baseline agent using message history as working memory showed some performance improvement but still failed to reliably solve even small mazes within a reasonable step budget. This suggests that current LLM architectures may need enhancements to effectively handle tasks involving persistent world state representation and reasoning in complex, partially observable environments.

items.title: Researchers present Self-GC, a self-governing context system for long-horizon LLM agents that manages lifecycle of context objects and reduces input tokens by up to 20% in production [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Self-GC, a self-governing context system designed for long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents to manage the lifecycle of context objects more effectively. Unlike traditional methods that rely on heuristics or summaries to handle accumulated data such as tool results and user constraints, Self-GC treats these elements as indexed objects and uses a side-channel planner to optimize folding, masking, and pruning actions. This approach significantly reduces input tokens while preserving the integrity of future continuations. In testing, Self-GC pruned nearly 44% of prefix tokens on a challenging dataset with minimal impact on subsequent outputs, outperforming heuristic baselines. In a larger production-derived suite, it achieved no-impact rates above 91%, compared to 77% to 87% for existing methods. Deployment in a production environment demonstrated daytime input token reductions of 10% to 15%, with peaks near 20%, highlighting the system's efficiency in runtime context management as opposed to post hoc text cleanup.

items.title: Researchers present SEA architecture for self-evolving agents with anytime-valid certificates that confine self-modification and provide auditable guarantees on a frozen base model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced SEA, a novel architecture designed for self-evolving agents that addresses the challenge of self-modification in learning systems. SEA confines changes to a small steering adapter and a versioned harness around a frozen base model, allowing modifications only through an anytime-valid gate that issues auditable certificates within a fixed error budget. This approach ensures that self-modifications are controlled and verifiable, maintaining the integrity of the base model's behavior. The architecture incorporates five loop controllers and verifier-in-the-loop mechanisms, such as best-of-N selection and self-repair, which provide dense, grader-free feedback derived solely from the task text. Evaluations on a 52-instance benchmark across four base models demonstrated that SEA improves performance by selecting among existing behaviors without regressions, with notable gains on strong base models. While results are based on single runs of costly evaluations, future work aims to address variability and optimize algorithm selection per task.

items.title: Researchers show divergent AI performance metrics affect whether frontier capabilities concentrate among wealthy actors or spread through smaller models, influencing policy decisions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have examined how different AI performance metrics influence whether advanced AI capabilities remain concentrated among wealthy developers or become accessible through smaller, less resource-intensive models. Their study shows that while some metrics indicate a narrowing performance gap between frontier and modest models, others reveal an ever-growing lead for frontier models. The distinction hinges on whether the metrics are bounded or unbounded, which affects how capabilities like software engineering or synthetic biology might spread or concentrate. The team provides mathematical conditions to classify performance metrics and highlights that many commonly used bounded metrics have closely related unbounded counterparts. This distinction is crucial for policy decisions, as bounded metrics suggest capabilities will diffuse broadly, whereas unbounded metrics imply concentration among a few actors with substantial resources. Understanding which metric best captures a domain's capabilities is essential for shaping effective AI governance and access strategies.

items.title: Researchers present Bayesian uncertainty propagation framework for Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines, evaluated on multi-hop question answering datasets StrategyQA and HotpotQA using GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4.1-Nano [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a Bayesian uncertainty propagation framework for Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems to estimate potential failures in multi-stage reasoning pipelines. This framework integrates uncertainty signals from planner, evaluator, and generator stages, which are combined through a Bayesian Network to assess system-level uncertainty and identify possible failure points. The approach was tested on multi-hop question answering datasets StrategyQA and HotpotQA using GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4.1-Nano models, demonstrating improved uncertainty estimation especially in HotpotQA where uncertainty accumulates across reasoning steps. The evaluation employed metrics such as AUROC, AUARC, Expected Calibration Error, and Brier Score to measure discrimination, selective prediction, and calibration. Results indicated that Bayesian propagation effectively captures uncertainty in complex reasoning tasks, though limitations were noted in StrategyQA due to miscalibration and unreliable upstream signals. This study suggests that Bayesian uncertainty propagation is a promising preliminary method for monitoring Agentic RAG systems, with further validation needed in practical applications like Offshore Wind maintenance decision support.

items.title: Researchers release PedNStream, an open-source Python simulator for scalable macroscopic pedestrian network flow with built-in control interfaces and validated large-scale performance
items.content_text: Researchers have developed PedNStream, an open-source Python simulator designed for scalable macroscopic pedestrian network flow. The tool is based on the Link Transmission Model and incorporates stochastic dynamics to capture variability in pedestrian movement. It features a utility-based route choice model and built-in interfaces for control interventions such as gating and route guidance, making it suitable for large-scale crowd management and feedback-based control scenarios. The simulator was evaluated through synthetic scenarios that tested key pedestrian flow mechanisms like queue formation and congestion dissipation, as well as real-network experiments that confirmed its consistency with observed pedestrian counts. A closed-loop case study demonstrated its capability for controller integration, and runtime analysis showed its scalability, establishing PedNStream as an efficient and practical platform for pedestrian network simulation and control.

items.title: Researchers present an automated multi-agent LLM pipeline that generates and verifies reaction classification rules, expanding taxonomy from 68 to 14,073 classes and classifying 97.7% of unseen reactions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed an automated multi-agent system using large language models (LLMs) to classify chemical reactions and generate corresponding classification rules. Applied to 665,901 US patent reactions, this pipeline expanded a traditional reaction taxonomy from 68 to 14,073 classes without human intervention and achieved classification of 97.7% of unseen reactions, matching the performance of leading proprietary classifiers while providing finer chemical resolution. The system operates through a verification loop that tests each generated rule against the reaction corpus, ensuring reliability. By combining this approach with a lightweight fingerprint classifier, the method adapts to new chemistries beyond its training data, creating a dynamic and self-expanding reactivity database. This work demonstrates a scalable route to transforming generative models into dependable symbolic systems for chemical synthesis planning.

items.title: Researchers formalize OpenAgent problem to study LLM agent generalization failures in dynamic tool use environments and propose Perturbation-Augmented Fine-Tuning to improve robustness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced the OpenAgent problem to study the challenges Large Language Model (LLM) agents face when generalizing in dynamic, real-world environments involving tool use. They formalize this setting by characterizing distributional shifts across queries, actions, observations, and domains, and create a controlled sandbox environment to systematically analyze these shifts across four levels: Perception, Interaction, Reasoning, and Internalization. Their experiments reveal that agents trained with Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning experience significant performance drops under such open environmental changes. To address these generalization issues, the team proposes Perturbation-Augmented Fine-Tuning, a method that introduces controlled disturbances during training to improve agent robustness and adaptability. This approach aims to enhance the practical utility of LLM agents in realistic, evolving scenarios. The researchers plan to release their code publicly to support further development in this area.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate a two-step method using constraint programming and task status dependencies to optimize resource utilization in autonomous laboratories for metal-organic framework synthesis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a two-step approach to optimize resource utilization in autonomous laboratories conducting metal-organic framework synthesis. The method first employs constraint programming to generate optimal schedules that minimize total experiment time while respecting hardware limitations and capacities. Then, a system of task status dependencies ensures the robust execution of these schedules, effectively managing multiple instruments with varying capacities and throughputs. This approach addresses the challenge of planning and executing experimental tasks in real-world settings where hardware constraints complicate resource management. By integrating scheduling optimization with task dependency tracking, the system enhances the efficiency and reliability of autonomous laboratory operations.

items.title: AutoMem framework automates memory management as a trainable skill in LLMs, doubling to quadrupling performance on long-horizon tasks across three games with a 32B parameter model [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed AutoMem, a framework that treats memory management in large language models (LLMs) as a trainable skill, significantly enhancing performance on long-horizon tasks. By integrating file-system operations as memory actions alongside task actions, the model autonomously manages its memory, improving both the structure supporting memory and the model's proficiency in using it. This approach doubled to quadrupled performance in three procedurally generated games using a 32-billion parameter model, achieving results comparable to leading systems like Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking. AutoMem operates through two automated loops: one where a strong LLM reviews and refines the memory structure based on complete agent trajectories, and another where the agent's effective memory decisions are used to directly train and enhance its memory skills. This method addresses the challenges of manual optimization in long-horizon tasks, where errors can remain hidden over thousands of steps, making human review impractical. The findings demonstrate that memory management is an independently learnable and high-impact skill for LLMs, offering a promising direction for improving their capabilities in complex, extended tasks without altering their core task-action behaviors.

items.title: UltraFlux introduces data-model co-design for native 4K text-to-image generation across diverse aspect ratios, outperforming open-source baselines on fidelity and aesthetics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: UltraFlux is a new approach to text-to-image generation that achieves high-quality native 4K resolution across various aspect ratios by addressing interconnected challenges in positional encoding, VAE compression, and optimization. Developed using a data-model co-design strategy, UltraFlux is trained on a large, diverse 4K image dataset with bilingual captions and metadata to enable resolution- and aspect ratio-aware sampling. The model integrates advanced techniques including Resonance 2D RoPE positional encoding, a non-adversarial VAE post-training scheme, an SNR-aware Huber Wavelet objective, and a stage-wise aesthetic curriculum learning method to enhance detail preservation and stability. UltraFlux demonstrates superior performance compared to strong open-source baselines on fidelity, aesthetics, and alignment metrics in multi-aspect ratio 4K settings, and with a large language model prompt refiner, it matches or exceeds the proprietary Seedream 4.0 model. This advancement represents a significant step forward in generating high-resolution, visually appealing images that generalize well across different formats.

items.title: Researchers evaluate Qwen- and Gemma-based LLMs for extracting RDF triples from conversational data to build Personal Knowledge Graphs for recommendation systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a reproducible pipeline that uses lightweight Large Language Models (LLMs) based on Qwen and Gemma to extract structured RDF triples from unstructured conversational data. This approach aims to build Personal Knowledge Graphs (PKGs) that model user preferences while preserving privacy. The study evaluates these models on their ability to generate RDF-compliant triples linked to Wikidata identifiers and assesses the quality of the extracted data in supporting recommendation systems. The evaluation focused on both the semantic accuracy of the triple extraction and the effectiveness of the resulting PKGs in downstream recommendation tasks. Results showed that some models achieved strong performance in extracting meaningful triples, which correlated with improved recommendation outcomes, demonstrating the potential of LLMs for constructing PKGs from conversational inputs.

items.title: Researchers present Topological Void Analysis, a mathematical framework identifying unexplored innovation opportunities in high-dimensional knowledge spaces, applied to 140,000 documents generating over 2,100 invention candidates [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Topological Void Analysis (TVA), a mathematical framework designed to identify unexplored innovation opportunities within complex, high-dimensional knowledge spaces. TVA defines topological voids as specific triads of concepts that are semantically related yet occupy unfilled regions in a hybrid embedding space, indicating potential areas for novel invention. Applying this method to approximately 140,000 documents, the team generated over 2,100 invention candidates across 96 target areas, with a high rate of quality validation through automated filtering and expert review. The framework operates by ensuring that concept pairs are both relevant to a domain anchor and sufficiently distinct to avoid obvious or unrelated combinations, while also sharing a sparse lexical connection. This approach allows TVA to uncover non-obvious connections that traditional keyword or citation-based methods might miss. Case studies demonstrate its effectiveness in surfacing innovative links rather than merely obvious related pairs, suggesting TVA's potential to systematically guide technical innovation discovery in dense research fields.

items.title: Researchers challenge cross-regime co-reference assumption in LLM individuation, proposing regime-indexed identity units based on experiments with Qwen3-4B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers challenge the common assumption in large language model (LLM) individuation that the same representational direction corresponds to the same content across different regimes such as prompt-conditioning, fine-tuning, and inference-time steering. Through experiments on Qwen3-4B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, they identify inconsistencies including non-collinearity of vectors, stronger displacement by fictional personas, biased mixtures influenced by training history, and asymmetric compositional behaviors that undermine this assumption. They propose a new framework called regime-indexed individuation, where identity is defined by a combination of representational vehicle and regime rather than by the vehicle alone. This approach reinterprets previous theoretical positions as describing distinct regime-specific objects rather than competing for a single referent, offering a revised perspective on LLM representation and individuation.

items.title: Researchers present BaRA, a BFS-and-Reflection web data collection agent that outperforms existing LLM-based agents on link discovery and multimodal extraction across synthetic and public websites [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed BaRA, a web data collection agent that combines bounded breadth-first search (BFS) traversal with history-based self-reflection to improve site-level data collection under fixed interaction limits. BaRA addresses common issues faced by large language model (LLM)-based web agents, such as missing relevant pages and incomplete multimodal outputs, by enhancing link discovery and extraction of downloadable media. The team evaluated BaRA on 50 synthetic websites with known reference sets and on three public sites with complex or dynamic layouts. BaRA outperformed existing methods including Pure LLM, SeeAct-Vision, and Browser-use, particularly excelling in recovering valid downloadable images and videos. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further use and development.

items.title: Researchers propose SchemaRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation framework that dynamically reduces large schemas for LLM-driven structured information extraction, improving accuracy by 8.8% and cutting latency and token costs by nearly half [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced SchemaRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation framework designed to improve structured information extraction from unstructured text using large language models (LLMs). SchemaRAG addresses challenges posed by large and complex target schemas by dynamically pruning the output schema space, which reduces prompt size and mitigates issues like increased cost, latency, and context length limits. This approach enhances extraction accuracy while optimizing resource use. The framework leverages schema metadata and few-shot examples to selectively reduce the schema during extraction tasks. Evaluations on healthcare and e-commerce datasets demonstrate that SchemaRAG achieves up to an 8.8% improvement in micro-F1 score, alongside a 47% reduction in latency and a 48% decrease in token costs. These results highlight SchemaRAG's effectiveness and practicality for handling large-schema extraction tasks with LLMs.

items.title: Researchers propose Loom, a three-layer assisted writing framework that controls narrative intent and rendering density to improve creative writing fidelity and descriptive intensity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Loom, a three-layer assisted writing framework designed to enhance creative writing by balancing narrative fidelity and descriptive intensity. Loom addresses a common issue in large language models where writing assistance either results in overly safe, superficial edits or uncontrolled plot expansions. By separating the generation of perceptual content from syntactic insertion, Loom maintains the original story structure while improving descriptive detail. The framework is based on a narratological distinction between story and discourse and uses an intent-centered semiotic chain-of-thought to precisely control narrative intent and rendering density. Evaluations using both automated metrics and human assessments show that Loom outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher overall quality with significant improvements in factual accuracy and descriptive richness.

items.title: Researchers propose a multi-objective framework to automatically optimize prompts for LLM-based user simulators in conversational recommender systems, improving behavioral alignment and addressing bias and data issues [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a multi-objective framework to automatically optimize prompts for large language model (LLM)-based user simulators in conversational recommender systems (CRSs). This approach aims to improve behavioral alignment with human interaction patterns while addressing challenges such as systematic positive bias, data leakage, and limited behavioral diversity that affect existing methods. The framework also reduces reliance on manual prompt engineering, which typically requires extensive domain expertise. Conversational recommender systems enable users to actively express preferences and adapt recommendations in real time, but evaluating these systems through human studies is costly and time-consuming. Additionally, obtaining CRS interaction data for training is difficult due to privacy concerns. LLM-based user simulators offer a promising solution by generating synthetic user interactions for both evaluation and training, and the proposed framework enhances their effectiveness across diverse prompt settings. Experimental results demonstrate that this automated prompt optimization framework outperforms baseline methods in producing user simulations that better reflect real human behaviors, potentially advancing the development and assessment of more accurate and reliable conversational recommender systems.

items.title: Researchers present SkillSelect-Serve, a budget-controllable and QoS-aware framework for skill service recommendation and composition in small LLM agents, improving utility over fixed top-k methods in tests with 35,353 skills [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed SkillSelect-Serve, a new framework designed to improve skill service recommendation and composition for small large language model (LLM) agents. Unlike traditional methods that return fixed top-k skill lists, SkillSelect-Serve offers budget control and quality of service (QoS) awareness by representing skills as structured services with detailed attributes such as dependencies, costs, risks, and QoS metrics. The framework translates natural language tasks into structured requirements and retrieves candidate services from a large registry, optimizing selection through dual-granularity utility modeling to balance coverage, redundancy, cost, and risk. Testing SkillSelect-Serve on a dataset of 35,353 skills and 586 task queries demonstrated consistent improvements in bundle recall and mean utility compared to fixed top-k retrieval methods. This approach enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of skill selection in LLM agents, potentially advancing their capability to handle complex tasks within specified resource constraints.

items.title: Researchers propose PRA-RAG, a provably robust aggregation algorithm for Retrieval-Augmented Generation that reduces poisoning attack success to 1% while maintaining 71% accuracy across benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed PRA-RAG, a provably robust aggregation algorithm designed to enhance the security of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems against poisoning attacks. These attacks manipulate retrieved texts to mislead Large Language Models (LLMs), which RAG uses to supplement external knowledge. PRA-RAG reduces the success rate of such attacks to 1% while maintaining 71% accuracy across various benchmarks, outperforming existing defense methods. PRA-RAG works by sampling multiple combinations of retrieved texts and leveraging geometric structures in the embedding space to identify a robust subset for stable aggregation. The researchers provide theoretical bounds on the maximum impact of poisoned content and introduce a quantitative measure of RAG's robustness. Experiments across different RAG architectures demonstrate the effectiveness of PRA-RAG in defending against retrieval corruption without compromising model performance.

items.title: Researchers introduce GRACE-RAG, a graph-augmented retrieval architecture for evidence synthesis that improves quality by up to 20% and enables lightweight deployment in closed-domain institutional settings [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed GRACE-RAG, a graph-augmented retrieval architecture designed to improve the quality of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems used in institutional question answering. GRACE-RAG shifts structural reasoning from the generative phase to a structured retrieval layer, which helps resolve ambiguities offline and supports deployment on lightweight, self-hosted models tailored to specific institutional vocabularies. This approach enhances evidence synthesis by up to 20% in quality, particularly in domains with dense entities and heterogeneous documents. Tests conducted with models of varying sizes, including Mistral 24B, GPT OSS 120B, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, demonstrated consistent improvements in completeness, depth, and anticipatory coverage. The findings suggest that the retrieval architecture plays a more critical role in structural quality than model scale, enabling reduced computational demands and latency without relying on proprietary systems.

items.title: Researchers propose an AI-based framework using large language models for automated compliance checks of multi-apartment floor plans under Australian building regulations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have proposed an AI-based framework to automate compliance checks of multi-apartment floor plans against Australian building regulations aimed at improving residents' well-being. The framework uses a Large Language Model (LLM) within a Rule Engine to translate textual building codes into executable rules, while a Data Extraction Engine processes floor plan images into structured building graphs. These graphs are then assessed by a Compliance Check Engine using the LLM-generated rules, enabling scalable and consistent evaluation of design features such as daylight access, ventilation, privacy, and space efficiency. This approach addresses challenges in current manual compliance checking, which is time-consuming and limited in scalability, as well as the fragmented nature of existing automated methods that typically focus on single apartments. By providing a unified, transparent system for multi-unit compliance assessment, the framework supports efficient enforcement of apartment design standards and promotes healthier, higher-density urban development across jurisdictions.

items.title: Researchers present Libra, a self-evolving framework that optimizes information retrieval environments using mutable catalogs and LLM-driven loops, improving code localization accuracy across 12 repositories [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Libra, a self-evolving framework designed to optimize information retrieval environments by introducing mutable catalogs-hierarchical Markdown files that serve as navigable indices-within code repositories. Libra operates through an LLM-driven loop where synthetic queries are generated, attempts are made to resolve them by navigating the catalogs, and the catalogs are rewritten in response to failures, leading to continuous improvements in code localization accuracy across 12 software engineering repositories. Evaluations show that this approach yields logarithmic gains in localization performance, and these improvements transfer effectively across different large language models and problem sets without additional training. The study also demonstrates that a minimalist coding agent using Libra-optimized catalogs outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, highlighting the potential of environment-focused optimization in agentic information retrieval systems. The code and datasets are publicly available for further research and development.

items.title: Researchers propose Profile-guided Personalized Retrieval Optimization to improve user-aware memory retrieval in long-term conversational agents, showing gains on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
