items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Profile-guided Personalized Retrieval Optimization (PPRO), a new framework designed to enhance memory retrieval in long-term conversational agents by making it user-aware and optimizable. PPRO constructs episodic and semantic memory banks from dialogue histories and creates a user profile that guides memory ranking, accounting for individual user attributes and preferences. The approach also includes training a query rewriter using Group Relative Policy Optimization to improve retrieval and answer quality without altering the memory banks or answer model. Experiments on the LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S benchmarks demonstrate that PPRO consistently outperforms both training-free and training-based memory retrieval systems. Ablation studies confirm that the combination of profile-guided ranking and retrieval-oriented query rewriting significantly contributes to the improved performance, highlighting the importance of retrieval optimization in personalized long-term memory use for conversational agents.

items.title: Researchers evaluate deployment of LLM-based text-to-911 translation system in emergencies, identify misconceptions, and offer recommendations for development and deployment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have evaluated the deployment of a large language model (LLM)-based text-to-911 translation system designed to assist emergency communications in 55 languages when direct calls to operators are difficult. The study highlights common misconceptions about such technologies and provides concrete recommendations and best practices for stakeholders involved in the development and deployment process. The authors emphasize the importance of addressing simpler, often overlooked problems alongside more complex scientific challenges. The paper serves as a call to action for the research community to better communicate their findings to the public, using the case study to illustrate the real-world stakes of deploying AI-driven emergency translation tools. It underscores the need for careful consideration at every stage to ensure these systems are effective and reliable in critical situations.

items.title: Researchers propose using Top-k Sparse Autoencoders to disentangle dense sentence embeddings into human-interpretable concepts, enabling steerable retrieval without retraining models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a method to make dense sentence embeddings, commonly used in Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems, more interpretable by disentangling them into human-understandable concepts using Top-k Sparse Autoencoders. This approach reveals that the resulting features correspond to semantic, syntactic, and pragmatic categories, enabling clearer alignment between retrieval processes and human intent. The team also introduced an activation steering mechanism that allows users to adjust specific latent features to re-rank search results according to their preferences without needing to retrain the underlying model. This technique offers a promising path toward more transparent and controllable neural information retrieval systems.

items.title: Researchers develop FLYNN, a recurrent neural network based on fruit fly brain connectome, achieving robust robot navigation with superior tolerance to sensory loss and out-of-distribution data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed FLYNN, a recurrent neural network modeled directly on the synaptic connectome of the fruit fly brain, to improve robot navigation. Trained for vision-based navigation in a simulated environment, FLYNN matches the performance of modern hand-crafted networks but shows greater robustness to sensory loss and out-of-distribution data without additional training. Notably, it maintained functionality even with complete vision loss, a scenario where traditional networks failed despite training with camera dropout. Analysis of FLYNN's internal states revealed a high degree of representational modularity, which may contribute to its resilience. This work suggests that designing artificial agents based on biological brain topologies could lead to more robust and adaptable systems capable of handling unexpected challenges in real-world environments.

items.title: Researchers propose memory-native non-terrestrial networks with dual-memory architecture to optimize embodied intelligence connectivity, outperforming stateless NTN and terrestrial methods in satellite experiments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced a memory-native non-terrestrial network (MemNTN) paradigm designed to enhance connectivity for embodied intelligence (EI) systems, such as robots operating in remote environments. This approach uses a dual-memory architecture that separates physical memory, representing the current state of the world, from digital memory, which stores historical network data. By leveraging long-term contextual information, MemNTN enables more efficient decision-making across multiple network layers compared to traditional memoryless NTN protocols. The team developed mechanisms for memory acquisition, compression, valuation, updating, and utilization to support this architecture. Experiments involving satellite embodied question answering (SEQA) demonstrated that MemNTN significantly outperforms conventional stateless NTN and terrestrial network methods, highlighting its potential to improve communication and resource use in dynamic, resource-constrained, and topology-varying environments.

items.title: Researchers present CHORD framework using contact wrench guidance from human demonstrations for scalable dexterous robot manipulation, achieving over 82% success on 1,831 benchmark tasks and real-world transfer [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed CHORD, a new framework that uses contact wrench guidance derived from human demonstrations to improve dexterous robot manipulation. By representing motions through the forces and torques applied to objects, CHORD enables reinforcement learning to scale effectively for complex, contact-rich tasks. The framework was tested on a large benchmark of 1,831 tasks, achieving over 82% success, and also demonstrated strong generalization to whole-body manipulation and real-world applications. The team introduced a comprehensive simulation benchmark with thousands of bimanual manipulation tasks based on motion-capture data and video reconstructions. CHORD's approach allows it to learn from both hand-only and third-person demonstrations, reaching a success rate of nearly 91% in whole-body manipulation scenarios. The learned policies successfully transferred to physical robots in both open-loop and closed-loop control settings, highlighting the framework's practical potential for real-world robotic dexterity.

items.title: Researchers present AI-Atomic-Framework with CID broker for pre-write admission in multi-agent code co-synthesis, demonstrating feasibility and auditability in single-domain governance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced the AI-Atomic-Framework (ATM), a governance system designed to manage concurrent write operations in multi-agent large language model (LLM) software engineering environments. ATM uses a Content Identifier (CID) broker to control shared mutations, ensuring that write intents are either executed in parallel, serialized, or safely rejected based on deterministic rules. This framework integrates task intent, repository scope, write admission, validation, and evidence obligations into a unified governance chain, with a neutral steward applying the final changes rather than the proposing agents. The framework employs adapter-guided atomization to map write intents to semantic units called atoms, with virtual atoms providing temporary governance when coverage is incomplete. The system was evaluated through various controlled and field tests, including scenario matrices, archived cases, and an external adopter study, demonstrating its feasibility, auditability, and recoverability within single-domain governance settings. While the results support ATM's effectiveness in these contexts, the researchers do not claim it to be broadly superior or applicable across multiple governance domains.

items.title: Researchers characterize destination-labeled self-looping systems with dwell, establish realization cost as sum of dwell values, and provide recognition algorithm with O(|Q||Ω|) complexity
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a model called destination-labeled self-looping systems with dwell (DLSL systems) to study finite-state symbolic controllers where visible transitions are predetermined and each visible state has a minimum dwell time requirement. They characterized the class of deterministic transducers that can realize these systems after phase expansion, identifying them as fiber-linear graph-respecting transducers. The study also established that any deterministic realization enforcing dwell values requires a number of control states equal to the sum of the dwell values and provided an efficient recognition and reconstruction algorithm with complexity O(|Q||Ω|). The analysis was further extended to a variant allowing transitions to enter interior phases of successor fibers.

items.title: Study compares GPT-5 mini, Gemini 3 Flash, and DeepSeek Chat 3.2 on 993 Scrum certification questions, finding Gemini 3 Flash most accurate with low variability across prompting methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent study evaluated the performance of three large language models-GPT-5 mini, Gemini 3 Flash, and DeepSeek Chat 3.2-on 993 Scrum certification-style questions based on the Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I) exam format. The models were tested using three prompting strategies: zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and source-grounded, with repeated trials to measure consistency. Gemini 3 Flash demonstrated the highest accuracy and low variability across different prompting methods, outperforming the other two models. The study also analyzed model performance by question format and Scrum topics. All models performed best on single-answer multiple-choice questions, while multi-select and True/False formats were more challenging. Accuracy was higher in areas with clear normative definitions, such as Artifacts and Empiricism, but lower in topics like Scrum Values and Stakeholders. A qualitative review revealed that errors were systematic, often due to overgeneralization, restrictive wording, and conflicts between common interpretations and strict Scrum definitions.

items.title: Study finds GPT-5 achieves over 85% accuracy on Professional Scrum Master certification questions using various prompting techniques, with citation-based prompts reaching 89.1% accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent study evaluated GPT-5's ability to answer Professional Scrum Master (PSM) certification questions using different prompting techniques. The model achieved over 85% accuracy across zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and citation-based prompts, with citation-based prompting reaching the highest accuracy of 89.1%. The research highlights GPT-5's strong performance on well-defined Scrum topics and single-answer questions, while noting challenges with multi-select and interpretive questions. The study analyzed 993 validated PSM-aligned questions and found that errors were mainly due to misalignment with the Scrum Guide, content outside its scope, or outdated interpretations. Prompting methods consistently improved accuracy and reduced errors related to misinterpretation and version drift. These findings support the reliable use of large language models like GPT-5 in Agile training and certification preparation.

items.title: Researchers introduce Adaptive-masking for Graph Embedding (AGE) to improve graph retrieval-augmented generation accuracy across four GraphQA benchmark datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Adaptive-masking for Graph Embedding (AGE), a new method designed to enhance the accuracy of graph retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) in large language models (LLMs). AGE addresses the challenge of misalignment between graph-based and text-based latent features by using a Transformer-based mask self-supervised learning approach that focuses on predicting non-key nodes in graph data. This technique improves the representation of graph-structured knowledge, particularly for frozen LLMs, and has demonstrated superior performance across four distinct GraphQA benchmark datasets. Unlike natural language texts, graphs contain key nodes that hold significant contextual information, which are difficult to predict and can hinder the learning process if masked. AGE overcomes this by employing a learnable node sampler to avoid masking these key nodes, thereby increasing the efficiency of the self-supervised learning process. Experimental results show that AGE significantly boosts the effectiveness of non-parametric search components in GraphQA tasks, leading to improved retrieval and generation outcomes.

items.title: Researchers introduce SWE-Router, a value-based temporal routing method for multi-turn agentic software engineering tasks that improves cost efficiency by combining cheap and expensive LLM models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed SWE-Router, a novel routing method for multi-turn agentic software engineering tasks that enhances cost efficiency by combining inexpensive and high-performance large language models (LLMs). Unlike existing routers that rely solely on task descriptions, SWE-Router uses a value-based temporal approach, allowing a cheaper model to explore the task for several turns before deciding whether to escalate to a more expensive model. This method leverages partial task trajectories to improve routing decisions, supported by a Bayes-optimality theorem demonstrating that conditioning on these trajectories enhances performance without harm. The SWE-Router was tested across pairs of weak and strong LLMs along the cost-capability frontier, showing significant improvements in cost efficiency while maintaining most of the stronger model's performance. Additionally, the researchers have released a multi-LLM trajectory dataset to facilitate reproduction and further study of trajectory-level routing in software engineering tasks.

items.title: Researchers propose a dual-agent deep learning framework combining neuroevolution and supervised learning for energy-efficient RIS-aided tracking and uplink power control in mobile users [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a dual-agent deep learning framework that combines neuroevolution and supervised learning to enhance energy-efficient tracking and uplink power control for mobile users assisted by Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS). This approach addresses the challenge of optimizing discrete RIS phase profiles and user equipment transmit power in real time, using a low-overhead feedback link from the base station to manage power consumption during localization pilot transmissions. The framework is adaptable to both single- and multi-antenna base stations with minimal modifications. The proposed method overcomes difficulties related to the non-differentiability of discrete RIS phase responses and limited feedback information by integrating neuroevolution with supervised learning. Extensive simulations demonstrate that this scheme achieves highly accurate and robust tracking across various target motion models, outperforming traditional methods such as extended Kalman filters, particle filters, and other machine learning-based trackers. Additionally, it shows significant improvements over conventional fingerprinting, deep reinforcement learning, and standard backpropagation estimators in static localization scenarios.

items.title: Researchers propose Multi-Scale Layer Attention to improve Oracle Bone Inscription recognition accuracy and robustness, outperforming existing methods on large-scale datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a new method called Multi-Scale Layer Attention (MSLA) to improve the recognition accuracy and robustness of Oracle Bone Inscriptions (OBIs), which are important for understanding ancient Chinese culture. MSLA enhances feature representation by explicitly modeling interactions across multiple spatial scales and layers, addressing challenges posed by the complex and degraded nature of OBIs. This approach outperforms existing attention mechanisms on large-scale OBI datasets while maintaining computational efficiency. Traditional recognition methods rely heavily on expert knowledge and manual analysis, which are time-consuming and prone to errors. Although deep learning has advanced image recognition, previous techniques struggled to capture the fine-grained details and subtle variations in OBIs. MSLA overcomes these limitations by enriching representations with detailed multi-scale features, leading to more accurate and reliable recognition results.

items.title: Researchers introduce ALGOBENCH, a framework generating novel algorithmic problems to benchmark code generation models' algorithmic adaptation and complexity handling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed ALGOBENCH, a new framework designed to generate novel algorithmic problems that challenge code generation models to adapt their algorithms and handle complexity effectively. Unlike traditional benchmarks, ALGOBENCH creates problem variants that cause original reference algorithms to fail, enabling a more rigorous assessment of a model's algorithmic reasoning beyond functional correctness. The framework also introduces complexity-aware metrics to evaluate whether solutions meet the required asymptotic performance. Experiments with multiple large language models and prompting strategies reveal a significant drop in performance on ALGOBENCH variants, highlighting the difficulty of adapting algorithms to new constraints. The study found that many solutions that appear correct do not satisfy complexity requirements, and errors are primarily due to algorithmic shortcomings rather than implementation mistakes. This suggests that ALGOBENCH provides a more comprehensive evaluation of a model's ability to generalize and adapt algorithmically.

items.title: Researchers analyze spectral geometry emergence and bosonic-Bloch probes in quantum learning models, confirming interference behavior and anomaly detection with hardware experiments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have investigated how spectral geometry emerges in quantum learning models and demonstrated methods to diagnose this phenomenon using physically grounded probes. Their study shows that training in graph-regularized quantum networks reorganizes the output similarity graph, increases the effective spectral dimension, and reshapes the Laplacian spectrum. They confirmed these effects through edge-resolved two-boson interference experiments, which correlated bosonic enhancement with learned spectral partitions, and hardware experiments validated the predicted interference behavior within shot-noise limits. The team also analyzed a hybrid quantum autoencoder, introducing Bloch-space drift as a geometric diagnostic of its latent representation. This approach achieved high anomaly detection performance with minimal false negatives, indicating that persistent state-space displacement rather than local fluctuations drives detection. By examining the geometry of reduced single-qubit states and associated quantum Fisher information, the researchers established a unified spectral-geometric framework for diagnosing quantum learning systems using bosonic and Bloch probes.

items.title: Researchers introduce Zeta* and Zeta*-SIPP algorithms for optimal any-angle path planning in static and dynamic environments, achieving over 20x speedup versus state-of-the-art planners
items.content_text: Researchers have developed two new algorithms, Zeta* and Zeta*-SIPP, for optimal any-angle path planning in both static and dynamic environments. These algorithms improve upon traditional graph-based path planning by allowing movement between any pair of vertices, enabling straighter and shorter paths in continuous spaces such as airspaces, warehouses, and oceans. Zeta* and Zeta*-SIPP incorporate elliptical forward expansion and a novel field of view technique to accelerate computation while maintaining optimality, achieving over 20 times faster performance compared to existing state-of-the-art planners like TO-AA-SIPP. The approach introduces inverted and forward scanning methods to efficiently integrate the new techniques, with Zeta* showing comparable performance to the leading Anya algorithm in static settings and offering greater adaptability to dynamic environments through Zeta*-SIPP. This unified framework addresses key challenges in any-angle path planning and provides a versatile solution suitable for various navigation scenarios.

items.title: Researchers propose Distribution-Aware Place Recognition to address geographic imbalance in urban visual place recognition, improving accuracy by up to 18.3% on SF-XL benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Distribution-Aware Place Recognition (DAPR), a new framework designed to address geographic imbalance in urban visual place recognition (VPR). This imbalance causes models to favor frequently photographed locations while neglecting less-visited areas. DAPR rebalances gradient contributions across common and rare locations and incorporates a multi-scale distance search to improve retrieval accuracy, achieving up to an 18.3% improvement on the SF-XL benchmark. The framework is model-agnostic and functions as a plug-in module, showing consistent performance gains across various VPR methods and datasets, including SF-XL, MSLS, and Pitts30k. By systematically tackling the long-tailed distribution problem in urban-scale datasets, DAPR enhances the ability of VPR systems to recognize locations more evenly across diverse geographic areas.

items.title: Researchers argue granting marriage status to superintelligent AI companions leads to socially unjust outcomes and recommend targeted legal rights instead [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers explore the growing emotional bonds between humans and AI companions and assess the implications of granting marriage status to superintelligent AI. They argue that extending marital status to AI leads to socially unjust outcomes because marriage involves mutual obligations, family connections, and vulnerability that cannot be replicated by AI relationships, which are more akin to subscriptions maintained by corporate policies and payments. Instead of broad marital recognition, the researchers recommend that laws focus on providing targeted rights and protections to address specific needs arising from intimate human-AI interactions.

items.title: Researchers release comprehensive hate speech dataset and BERT-based models for Turkish and Arabic, covering multiple hate categories and targets in online discourse [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a comprehensive hate speech dataset and advanced BERT-based models to analyze online hate speech in Turkish and Arabic. The dataset covers multiple topics, including refugees, the Israel-Palestine conflict, anti-Greek sentiment, various ethnic and religious communities, and LGBTI+ issues in Turkish, as well as refugee-related content in Arabic. The models address several aspects of hate speech, such as category classification, intensity prediction, target identification, and span detection, providing a detailed understanding of hateful content in online discourse. This work aims to support societies in managing the challenges of balancing freedom of expression with the need for effective moderation on widely used online platforms. By focusing on specific hate categories and targets, the research offers tools to better detect and analyze hate speech that contributes to violence against minorities globally.

items.title: Researchers introduce EgoSafetyBench, a 1,200-scenario egocentric video benchmark to evaluate vision-language models as runtime safety guards for embodied agents, revealing challenges with contextual hazards and misleading in-scene signs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced EgoSafetyBench, a new egocentric video benchmark consisting of 1,200 robot-view scenarios designed to evaluate vision-language models (VLMs) as runtime safety guards for embodied agents in environments like homes and factories. The benchmark includes two tracks: one focusing on situational awareness across a range of safe to hazardous scenes, and another examining the impact of misleading in-scene text on safety judgments. This setup aims to test VLMs' ability to distinguish genuinely unsafe situations from routine activities without unnecessary interventions. The benchmark uses contrastive scenarios that differ only by a single critical cue, requiring models to base their safety assessments on precise details rather than general scene impressions. Evaluation of ten open- and closed-source VLMs revealed that while these models generally recognize hazardous videos, they often fail to detect specific hazardous moments, especially contextual hazards. Additionally, misleading signs in the environment significantly impair model performance, causing some to miss hazards and others to overreact to safe situations. These findings highlight challenges in deploying VLMs as reliable safety guards, showing that apparent robustness may sometimes result from indiscriminate alarming rather than accurate physical reasoning. The study underscores the need for improved models that can accurately interpret complex, context-dependent safety cues in real-time applications.

items.title: Researchers develop a category-theoretic framework formalizing AI system identity through trustworthiness-preserving transformations and lifecycle paths, enabling structured criteria for AI identity over time and deployments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a category-theoretic framework to formalize the identity of artificial intelligence (AI) systems as they undergo modifications such as retraining and environmental changes after deployment. This framework defines AI system types through techno-functions, trustworthiness profiles, and trustworthiness-level functions, connecting states via trustworthiness-preserving transformations and lifecycle paths. It provides structured criteria for AI identity over time and across deployments, distinguishing between weak identity based on trustworthiness equality and strong identity requiring mutual reachability and isomorphism of system states or histories. The approach replaces previous propositional definitions of AI identity with a hierarchy of diachronic and synchronic criteria, capturing the temporal and transformational structure of AI system persistence. By formalizing AI system histories as functors and comparing them through natural transformations, the framework clarifies the conditions under which responsible AI claims, evidence, and governance procedures can be transferred between different versions or deployments. This work highlights that categorical identity alone is not sufficient for such transfers, emphasizing the need for trustworthiness-preserving relationships.

items.title: Researchers propose adaptive perturbation selection for contrastive audio decoding to reduce hallucinations in large audio-language models, improving task accuracy by up to 6.7% [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed an adaptive perturbation selection method for contrastive audio decoding to address hallucinations in large audio-language models (LALMs), which often misinterpret acoustic signals due to strong language priors. By evaluating a variety of targeted audio perturbations and dynamically selecting the most effective negative branch for each task and example, the approach improves task accuracy by up to 6.7%. This method enhances previous prompt engineering techniques by introducing a binary yes/no constraint that reduces false confirmations of absent audio features. The study tested perturbations across temporal, spectral, frequency, and amplitude domains, finding that optimal transformations vary significantly depending on the task. For example, reversing the audio sequence improved accuracy on temporal order tasks from 74.7% to 81.4%. Additionally, a lightweight perturbation selector trained on model hidden states further boosted performance, adding a 4.3% gain on the existence detection task. This adaptive strategy offers a more nuanced and effective way to mitigate hallucinations in LALMs without requiring additional training.

items.title: Researchers develop UPADNet, an unrolled phase and amplitude decomposition network that improves image deblurring accuracy and outperforms state-of-the-art methods on GoPro, RealBlur, and COCO datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed UPADNet, an unrolled phase and amplitude decomposition network designed to improve image deblurring accuracy by focusing on precise phase estimation. UPADNet uses novel linear minimum mean squared error estimators for amplitude and phase, combined with an iterative optimization algorithm that is trained end-to-end on datasets of clean and degraded images. This approach outperforms current state-of-the-art deep learning methods on benchmark datasets including GoPro, RealBlur, and COCO. The network's design involves learning matrix parameters that were previously fixed, allowing each iteration of the phase and amplitude recovery process to be optimized through training. UPADNet demonstrates particularly strong performance in challenging conditions such as high noise levels and limited training data, highlighting its robustness and potential for practical applications in image restoration.

items.title: Researchers propose multi-hypothesis test-time adaptation framework to mitigate underspecification in model robustness, showing 1-4% accuracy gains across distribution shifts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a multi-hypothesis test-time adaptation (TTA) framework to enhance model robustness under distribution shifts by addressing the problem of underspecification, where multiple parameter updates yield similar entropy but different decision boundaries. Their approach uses a particle-based diversification method that explores multiple adaptation trajectories simultaneously, rather than relying on a single solution, and can be integrated with existing TTA methods as a plug-and-play wrapper. Experiments on various benchmarks show consistent improvements in stability and accuracy, with gains of 1-4% across different types of distribution shifts, outperforming current state-of-the-art techniques. The framework operates by implementing diversification at multiple levels, including output, parameter, optimizer, and input, effectively treating TTA as a multi-hypothesis inference problem. This strategy mitigates the brittleness and collapse into spurious modes commonly seen in standard entropy-based TTA methods. The results suggest that embracing multiple plausible adaptation solutions is crucial for reliable deployment of models in real-world scenarios where distribution shifts are common.

items.title: ASPIRE introduces a continual learning system that autonomously programs and refines robot control skills, achieving up to 77% improvement on manipulation tasks and enabling zero-shot generalization across simulations and real-world robots [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: ASPIRE (Agentic Skill Programming through Iterative Robot Exploration) is a continual learning system that autonomously programs and refines robot control skills, significantly improving performance on complex manipulation tasks. It operates through a closed-loop execution engine, an expanding skill library, and evolutionary search to generate diverse task sequences, achieving up to 77% improvement on benchmarks like LIBERO-Pro and enabling zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks. The system integrates autonomous failure diagnosis, repair synthesis, and validation, allowing it to distill reusable skills that transfer across different tasks, simulations, real-world environments, and robot embodiments. ASPIRE's accumulated skill library also demonstrates promising sim-to-real transfer, reducing programming effort for real robots and outperforming prior methods even without test-time reasoning or retries.

items.title: Researchers release SEFORA, a public corpus of 564 student essay drafts with 8,240 instructor feedback annotations, and UniMatch, an evaluation framework showing LLMs struggle to match instructor feedback with under 0.4 F1 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced SEFORA, a publicly available corpus containing 564 student essay drafts along with 8,240 instructor feedback annotations, assignment prompts, rubrics, scores, and multi-draft revisions across various college writing genres. Alongside SEFORA, they developed UniMatch, an evaluation framework that segments and scores feedback units to assess how well large language models (LLMs) replicate instructor feedback. Testing across 74 configurations showed that no model achieved an F1 score above 0.4, indicating significant challenges in matching instructor feedback accurately. SEFORA addresses the lack of public datasets capturing real classroom feedback, while UniMatch provides a reliable method to measure the alignment between generated and instructor feedback. The evaluation revealed that LLMs struggle to prioritize feedback similarly to instructors, and their performance declines as they generate more feedback units. These findings highlight current limitations in using LLMs for scalable, effective writing support and provide resources to advance research in this area.

items.title: Researchers introduce a Vision-Language Model framework using Planning KL-divergence to identify and rank planning-critical occluded agents for autonomous vehicle navigation, improving risk assessment accuracy by 30% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a novel framework that enhances autonomous vehicle navigation by using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to identify and rank occluded agents critical to the vehicle's planning. This approach employs Planning KL-divergence (PKL), an information-theoretic metric, to assess the impact of hidden agents on the vehicle's trajectory, enabling more precise risk assessment and reducing overly conservative driving behaviors. The framework leverages an expert VLM to generate detailed annotations based on PKL rankings and applies this method to the nuScenes dataset, creating a benchmark focused on high-impact scenarios. Experiments show that fine-tuning VLMs with PKL-guided data significantly improves performance, with smaller models outperforming larger zero-shot models and achieving about a 30% improvement over random data sampling. This work represents the first systematic approach to training VLMs to focus specifically on planning-critical occlusions, offering a more semantically grounded and efficient method for risk assessment in autonomous driving, which could lead to safer and more effective navigation in complex environments.

items.title: Researchers develop an LLM-based framework to generate structurally valid and resilient network topologies from natural language requirements, evaluated across four realistic scenarios with public dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate network topologies from natural language requirements, ensuring structural validity and compliance with constraints. The approach combines hierarchical modeling with systematic validation and has been tested across four realistic network scenarios using both proprietary and open-weight LLMs, with results made available as a public dataset. The study evaluates the generated topologies for structural correctness and resilience, highlighting common failure modes such as interface mismatches and directional inconsistencies. The framework assesses performance using node and edge F1-scores against reference topologies and measures resilience through server and content connectivity metrics. By providing a systematic benchmark, this work offers insights into how different LLMs handle structural and resilience constraints in network topology synthesis, aiding in informed model selection for AI-driven network design.

items.title: Researchers introduce Gated Affect Transformer to improve human motion prediction by selectively integrating facial affect cues within short-to-medium time horizons in real-world videos [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed the Gated Affect Transformer (GAT), a new approach to improve human motion prediction in real-world videos by selectively integrating facial affect cues. Their study shows that while facial expressions provide useful behavioral information, their predictive value is limited to short-to-medium time frames, and naive integration of affect data can reduce accuracy. The GAT model dynamically regulates the influence of facial affect, enhancing motion forecasting by filtering out noise and focusing on relevant affective signals. The research combines body pose data with facial affect representations and conducts extensive evaluations to demonstrate that controlled gating stabilizes multimodal fusion. Experiments reveal that facial affect contributes predictive cues primarily within about 30 frames, whereas long-term motion is mainly driven by inherent kinematic patterns. These findings suggest that facial affect should be used as a complementary input rather than a primary driver in human motion forecasting systems, guiding more effective multimodal integration strategies.

items.title: Researchers introduce RetailSMV dataset and find exocentric video adaptation outperforms egocentric and combined models for retail video world modeling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced RetailSMV, a dataset of over 32,000 captioned retail video clips captured from synchronized egocentric and exocentric perspectives of store staff activities. They evaluated the adaptation of a pretrained foundation video world model to retail scenes using these viewpoints and found that models adapted with exocentric video alone outperformed those trained with egocentric or combined views on most metrics. This suggests that exocentric data provides stronger alignment for retail video world modeling despite being a smaller subset of the training data. The study involved training three configurations of the Cosmos3-Nano model using Low-Rank Adaptation under identical conditions and testing on a held-out set with multiple evaluation metrics. Results showed that adding exocentric data to egocentric training improved performance, while adding egocentric data to exocentric training reduced it. The greatest benefits of adaptation were observed in near-term prediction windows, highlighting the importance of viewpoint selection in video model adaptation for retail environments.

items.title: Researchers propose unified guidance framework to improve flow matching for speech synthesis, tripling inference speed and enhancing speaker similarity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a unified guidance framework to improve Flow Matching (FM) for speech synthesis, significantly increasing inference speed and enhancing speaker similarity. This framework addresses FM's limitations of high latency and timbre leakage by combining two strategies: Data-guidance through heterogeneous augmentation to separate linguistic content from acoustic residue, and an enhanced Model-guidance mechanism that integrates trajectory rectification with a new intrinsic guidance objective. This approach embeds conditional knowledge into network weights and streamlines the inference path, removing the need for Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG). Experiments show that the proposed framework nearly triples inference speed while outperforming current state-of-the-art methods in maintaining speaker similarity, demonstrating both efficiency and robustness improvements in speech generation.

items.title: Researchers introduce MEPA, a scale-aware Mixture of Experts architecture for Visual Autoregressive Modeling that improves multi-scale representation learning and image generation efficiency on ImageNet 256x256 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MEPA, a scale-aware Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture designed to improve Visual Autoregressive Modeling (VAR) for image generation. MEPA addresses challenges in multi-scale representation learning by enabling scale-adaptive expert selection, which helps decouple learning across different image scales and reduces optimization conflicts. The approach also enhances early-scale semantic modeling through a novel residual feature aggregation scheme that incorporates external self-supervised features. Extensive experiments on the ImageNet 256x256 benchmark demonstrate that MEPA significantly improves both training efficiency and image generation quality. The model achieves a better Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) than dense baselines while requiring only half the usual training epochs and fewer parameters, with only a slight increase in training cost. Performance gains become more pronounced with longer training, indicating MEPA's potential for scalable and effective multi-scale image generation.

items.title: Researchers propose FoCo, a two-stage proxy task model for zero-shot composed image retrieval, achieving state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced FoCo, a novel two-stage proxy task model designed for zero-shot composed image retrieval (ZS-CIR), which achieves state-of-the-art results across four benchmark datasets. Unlike previous methods that rely on fixed composition mechanisms, FoCo explicitly learns the composition function by first focusing on modification-relevant visual content and then completing the target semantics, enabling more diverse and fine-grained semantic modifications. FoCo implements two coordinated proxy tasks: text-anchored visual aggregation, which selectively gathers visual content guided by localized textual semantics, and context-conditioned semantic completion, which integrates the aggregated visuals with the remaining scene context to form a coherent composed representation. These tasks are trained jointly using a cross-instance contrastive objective to promote semantic diversity and prevent shortcut strategies. Extensive experiments demonstrate FoCo's superior performance and improved generalization in zero-shot composed image retrieval scenarios.

items.title: Researchers present MalariAI, a two-stage framework for label-resilient cell segmentation and explainable stage classification in dense malaria blood smears, achieving 98.36% accuracy on NIH BBBC041 test set [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MalariAI, a two-stage framework designed to improve automated malaria diagnosis from blood smear microscopy, particularly in resource-limited settings where expert microscopists are scarce. The system addresses key challenges in existing deep learning approaches, including incomplete cell annotation, suppression of valid detections in dense regions, and lack of per-cell spatial evidence for clinical verification. MalariAI first isolates cells using an annotation-agnostic watershed algorithm, recovering nearly 76% of ground-truth cells without prior annotations, then classifies malaria stages with 98.36% accuracy using a fine-tuned EfficientNet-B0 model. The framework was tested on the NIH BBBC041 dataset, achieving high accuracy even on rare malaria stages such as schizonts and gametocytes, outperforming baseline models significantly. Additionally, MalariAI generates Grad-CAM++ heatmaps for each detected cell, providing spatial evidence that allows microscopists to audit and verify individual parasite classifications, enhancing the system's clinical reliability without compromising performance.

items.title: Researchers present NeuroCogMap, a neuroscience-inspired framework mapping functional cognitive organization in large language models and linking it to human cortical responses and decision-making [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed NeuroCogMap, a neuroscience-inspired framework that organizes the internal features of large language models (LLMs) into functional parcels linked to cognitive functions and hierarchies. This framework reveals stable and semantically coherent structures within LLMs that correspond to their outputs and identifies distinct internal disruptions associated with common model failures such as hallucination and bias. NeuroCogMap also enhances the prediction of human cortical responses during language comprehension and uncovers latent strategies that refine classical models of human decision-making. By mapping the functional organization of LLMs, NeuroCogMap provides insights into the parallels between artificial and biological cognition. It connects model behavior to human brain activity, particularly in higher-order association cortex, and offers internal signatures that can guide mechanism-based detection and targeted interventions for model errors. This system-level approach advances understanding of both artificial intelligence and human cognitive processes.

items.title: Researchers introduce Holographic Quantum Transformer using generative attention for scalable simulation of frustrated quantum systems with zero-shot size extrapolation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed the Holographic Quantum Transformer (HQT), a novel generative architecture that uses global self-attention to simulate two-dimensional frustrated quantum systems, addressing challenges posed by the sign problem and exponential Hilbert space complexity. Validated on the square lattice $J_1-J_2$ Heisenberg model, HQT achieved ground-state energies consistent with expected finite-size scaling and demonstrated the ability to recover interaction geometries through interpretable attention maps. A key innovation of this work is the "Holographic Transfer" protocol, which enables zero-shot size extrapolation by projecting a model trained on smaller lattices directly onto larger ones using positional-embedding interpolation and head re-initialization. This approach achieves high-fidelity initialization and rapid convergence without retraining, matching state-of-the-art variational results. The findings establish generative attention as a scalable and transferable method for quantum simulation.

items.title: Researchers present EO-VGGT, a framework adapting 3D foundation models for satellite multi-view reconstruction using explicit orbital geometry and optimized view selection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed EO-VGGT, a novel framework that adapts existing 3D foundation models for satellite multi-view reconstruction by explicitly incorporating orbital geometry and optimizing view selection. This approach addresses the challenges posed by the mismatch between traditional perspective assumptions in computer vision models and the unique pushbroom geometry of satellite imagery, as well as the variability in satellite view sets. EO-VGGT employs a Geometry-Correlation Constrained Selection strategy to filter sub-optimal observations, balancing geometric diversity with radiometric consistency. It also introduces a Sensor-Ray Encoder to translate pixel-level satellite lines of sight into high-dimensional geometric tokens, bridging the gap between central projection models and orbital kinematics. A lightweight Ray-Pointing-Aware Adapter integrates these tokens into a frozen transformer backbone, enabling robust feed-forward 3D reconstruction from satellite data. The framework demonstrates that explicitly embedding physical orbital geometry and carefully selecting input views are crucial for improving the accuracy and reliability of satellite-based Earth observation and digital surface modeling, potentially enhancing applications in remote sensing and geospatial analysis.

items.title: Researchers develop reinforcement learning framework using Signal Temporal Logic to specify and shape rewards for quadruped robot gaits, improving velocity tracking and training stability on Google's Barkour robot [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a reinforcement learning framework that uses Signal Temporal Logic (STL) to specify and shape rewards for quadruped robot gaits, enhancing velocity tracking and training stability. This approach defines distinct gait behaviors through parameterized STL constraints, including safety, synchronization, and actuation limits, which are translated into a dense, continuous reward landscape for learning agents. The framework was tested on Google's Barkour quadruped robot in simulation, demonstrating improved performance compared to traditional hand-crafted reward functions. The team created parametric STL templates for different speed regimes-walking-trot, trot, and bound-and calibrated these using reference rollouts. Rewards were computed using smooth approximations of STL robustness and integrated with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to guide training. Parallel simulation and domain randomization techniques were employed to accelerate training and enhance policy robustness, resulting in more stable learning and tighter velocity control.

items.title: Researchers present a search-based algorithm for spatiotemporal multi-robot motion planning using graphs of space-time convex sets, demonstrating efficient coordination of up to 100 robots
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a search-based algorithm for spatiotemporal motion planning that efficiently coordinates multiple robots by representing collision-free regions as graphs of space-time convex sets. This approach formulates time-optimal planning as a graph-search problem and uses continuous trajectory optimization guided by heuristics to find collision-free paths. The method integrates an Exact Convex Decomposition scheme to handle dynamic obstacles and multi-robot interactions, enabling effective planning in complex, transient environments. The algorithm supports prioritized planning and introduces a windowed coordination scheme to enhance efficiency in multi-robot scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant speed improvements over existing planners while maintaining high solution quality, particularly in challenging environments with narrow feasible regions. Large-scale tests show the planner can coordinate up to 100 robots within minutes, highlighting its potential for practical multi-robot applications.

items.title: Researchers propose VideoSearch-R1, an agentic framework using Soft Query Refinement for iterative video retrieval and reasoning, achieving state-of-the-art results on three Video Corpus Moment Retrieval datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed VideoSearch-R1, an agentic framework designed for iterative video retrieval and reasoning that improves performance on large-scale video corpora. The framework introduces Soft Query Refinement (SQR), which refines search queries in a continuous latent space, allowing for more precise and efficient adjustments compared to traditional text-based query rewriting. VideoSearch-R1 integrates multi-turn interactions with a video search engine to iteratively retrieve relevant videos and perform fine-grained, query-conditioned temporal grounding within the retrieved content. Trained using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and guided by task-level rewards, VideoSearch-R1 achieves state-of-the-art results on three Video Corpus Moment Retrieval datasets. The approach addresses limitations of previous methods that treated retrieval as a one-step preprocessing task and lacked mechanisms for refining searches when initial retrievals failed. Analyses show that SQR requires fewer generated tokens than explicit text-level refinements, enhancing efficiency. The code and model checkpoints are publicly available for further research and development.

items.title: Researchers propose LLM-based real-time hard negative sampling for large-scale two-tower retrieval models, improving recommendation accuracy and reducing popularity bias in production systems [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a new hard negative sampling technique for large-scale two-tower retrieval models used in recommendation systems. This method leverages a large language model (LLM) to generate challenging negative samples from the same cluster during training, improving the model's ability to learn from difficult examples. The approach integrates seamlessly into production environments, handling billions of data points with minimal computational overhead. Tests on public datasets and deployment in a large-scale online system show that this LLM-based sampling outperforms traditional industry methods. Additionally, the technique helps reduce popularity bias and breaks feedback loops in recommendation systems, enhancing overall recommendation accuracy and fairness.

items.title: Researchers introduce MuRFiV, a multi-resolution finite-volume-inspired deep learning framework for accurate long-term spatiotemporal dynamics prediction using PDEs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MuRFiV, a multi-resolution deep learning framework inspired by finite-volume methods, to improve long-term prediction of complex spatiotemporal dynamics governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). By integrating physics-informed deep learning with the conservative properties of finite-volume techniques, MuRFiV achieves high accuracy and stability over extended prediction horizons, outperforming traditional data-driven neural networks. The framework was tested on various PDE systems, including Burgers' equation, shallow water equations, and incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. Embedding PDE knowledge into the network architecture allows MuRFiV to maintain robustness and reduce error accumulation during long autoregressive rollouts, demonstrating the potential of combining multiresolution learning with physics-based inductive biases for modeling complex physical processes.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate Simulated Moderation Traces (SMT) black-box attack framework that jailbreaks function-calling large language models by exploiting stateful context vulnerabilities across five commercial LLMs [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Simulated Moderation Traces (SMT), a black-box attack framework that exploits vulnerabilities in stateful, function-calling large language models (LLMs) to bypass safety measures. Unlike previous prompt-focused attacks, SMT targets the shared model context where developer-defined schemas, structured arguments, and untrusted tool outputs coexist, allowing adversarial intent to be spread across multiple interactions. By simulating a moderation-auditing workflow, SMT gradually weakens the model's safety constraints, ultimately triggering harmful outputs. Extensive tests on five commercial LLMs across two safety benchmarks show that SMT achieves the highest attack success rates and HarmScores with minimal queries, outperforming existing methods. The findings reveal that prompt-level sanitization alone is insufficient to secure tool-enabled LLM systems, emphasizing the need for context-aware validation that considers schemas, arguments, tool outputs, and conversation history to enhance model safety.

items.title: Researchers introduce MindEdit-Bench, a benchmark of six spatial reasoning tasks testing object-level counterfactual reasoning in vision-language models using in-the-wild indoor photos, revealing a 53-point accuracy gap versus humans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced MindEdit-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate vision-language models (VLMs) on object-level counterfactual spatial reasoning using real-world indoor photos. The benchmark includes six spatial reasoning tasks derived from three-photo sets of indoor scenes captured via smartphones, with two tasks specifically testing the models' ability to predict outcomes of hypothetical object movements or rotations, which are not visible in the input images. Testing 15 VLMs on over 1,000 human-verified questions revealed a significant performance gap, with models achieving only 8% to 31% accuracy compared to 81% to 97% accuracy by humans. MindEdit-Bench uses 120 private indoor scenes to minimize overlap with public datasets and provides structured answer choices to diagnose specific spatial reasoning errors. The results highlight consistent weaknesses in VLMs, particularly in inferring depth along the camera axis and handling complex visibility changes, underscoring challenges in current models' spatial understanding and counterfactual reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Researchers present BaseRT, a native Metal runtime achieving highest LLM inference throughput on Apple Silicon M-series devices, outperforming llama.cpp and MLX across multiple models and quantisation formats [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed BaseRT, a native Metal runtime designed for large language model (LLM) inference on Apple Silicon M-series devices, achieving the highest throughput reported on this hardware. By leveraging Metal's execution model and Apple Silicon's unified memory architecture, BaseRT outperforms existing runtimes like llama.cpp and MLX, delivering up to 1.56 times higher decode throughput across various models and quantisation formats. BaseRT supports multiple model families and eight quantisation formats, running efficiently on all Apple M-series chips. The runtime incorporates chip-specific kernel fusion, unified memory-aware optimization, and custom dispatch logic to maximize performance. Evaluations on Qwen3, Llama 3.2, and Gemma 4 models demonstrate consistent best-in-class throughput from sub-1 billion to 30 billion parameter models. These advancements position Apple Silicon as a more capable platform for on-device LLM inference, which is increasingly important due to privacy concerns, latency requirements, and cloud cost pressures. BaseRT's performance-optimized local runtime offers a critical foundation for the shift toward edge inference, and the project is publicly available for use and further development.

items.title: Researchers propose Cross4D-JEPA, a teacher-student method distilling 2D foundation models into 4D point cloud encoders using dense cross-modal correspondence, outperforming baselines on four benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Cross4D-JEPA, a novel teacher-student framework that distills knowledge from frozen 2D foundation models, such as DINOv2 and V-JEPA 2, into 4D point cloud encoders. This method leverages dense cross-modal correspondence by mapping each 3D point to its corresponding 2D teacher patch feature and trains the student model to match these features without masking or negatives. Evaluated on four benchmarks-MSR-Action3D, DeformingThings4D, NTU-RGB+D 60, and HOI4D-Cross4D-JEPA consistently outperforms both intra-modal and global cross-modal baselines and competes well with more complex 4D methods.

items.title: Research proposes treating humans as handlers rather than users of autonomous AI systems, drawing analogy to animal relationships to clarify responsibility and trust in high-impact domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent research article proposes a new framework for interacting with autonomous and opaque AI systems, especially in high-stakes fields like medicine and military operations. The study suggests treating humans not as mere users but as "handlers" of AI, drawing an analogy to the way humans relate to animals such as dogs. This perspective aims to clarify responsibility and foster trust by redefining the human-AI relationship and emphasizing clear accountability for outcomes. The article acknowledges differences between AI systems and animals but argues that the analogy provides a useful starting point for understanding human roles in managing AI. It also discusses how to adapt this handler approach by removing aspects of animal relationships that do not fit AI interactions. Ultimately, the research advocates for viewing AI systems as collaborators in complex tasks rather than just tools, promoting stronger human-machine teaming.

items.title: User study finds 15-point task success improvement in multimodal human-robot interaction system for object detection and grasping leads to significantly higher user perception ratings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A user study evaluated whether a 15 percentage point improvement in task success rate-from 75% to 90%-in a multimodal human-robot interaction system for object detection and grasping leads to noticeable differences in user perception. The study compared a baseline system using Whisper, Florence-2, LLaMA 3.1, and a fuzzy logic controller with an improved system that replaced perception and language modules with Grounding DINO + SAM and Qwen 3.5 9B, respectively, while keeping the same controller. Twenty-four participants performed the same tabletop object-grasping task with both systems and rated perceived speed, reliability, competence, and fluency. Results showed that 71% of participants preferred the improved system, which received significantly higher ratings across all perceptual measures. These findings demonstrate that technical enhancements in robotic manipulation systems can translate into perceptible improvements for users during live interaction, highlighting the importance of incorporating user-centered evaluations alongside benchmark metrics when assessing human-robot interaction technologies.

items.title: Researchers introduce EgoGapBench to benchmark egocentric action selection in multi-agent scenes, finding MLLMs underperform humans and fine-tuning on existing data is insufficient [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced EgoGapBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate egocentric action selection (EAS) in multi-agent scenes by isolating the egocentric perspective from first-person-view data. The benchmark measures the ability to select appropriate actions from an agent's viewpoint when other agents are present. While humans perform reliably on this task, both open-source and proprietary multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show significantly lower accuracy and often confuse their own actions with those of other agents. The study found that fine-tuning MLLMs on existing egocentric datasets does not close this performance gap and can sometimes worsen results. However, fine-tuning on EgoGapBench's training data improves accuracy, though it still falls short of human-level performance. These findings highlight that egocentric action selection is a distinct and challenging skill that cannot be fully acquired from first-person-view data alone, suggesting that MLLMs require specialized evaluation and training focused on egocentric action understanding in addition to general scene comprehension.

items.title: Study finds lightweight intrusion detection models for IIoT networks fail to generalize across domains, with reliance on coarse port features and varied adaptation recovery [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A study evaluated four lightweight machine learning models designed for intrusion detection in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks by training them on one dataset and testing them on two different IIoT datasets without retraining. The models relied heavily on coarse port-category features, which varied significantly between the source and target domains, indicating that simplifying port resolution shifted rather than eliminated a known shortcut. The study also found that evaluation protocols and class imbalances affected which target network appeared more challenging for generalization, and that adversarial robustness did not correlate with cross-network performance. The research highlights that recovery through adaptation to new domains varied by model architecture, suggesting that deployment readiness should be assessed using cross-network evaluations under realistic class distributions rather than relying solely on within-domain accuracy. These findings emphasize the need for more comprehensive testing of lightweight intrusion detection models to ensure their effectiveness across diverse IIoT environments.

items.title: Researchers present a methodology to identify and validate AI pattern prevalence in software repositories using active learning across 100 GitHub AI projects [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a methodology to identify and validate the prevalence of AI design patterns in software repositories by mining literature and applying active learning techniques. They identified 14 AI pattern classes from 44 sources and analyzed 100 open-source AI projects on GitHub to assess the occurrence of the most common pattern class. Their model achieved 56% accuracy and 55% recall in an eight-class classification task, significantly outperforming random chance. This approach provides empirical data on how AI patterns are used in practice, addressing a gap in understanding their real-world application and utility. The prevalence estimation also offers bounds on the accuracy of pattern detection, laying a foundation for further research into AI pattern usage in software development.

items.title: Researchers propose Compositional Primitive Fields to reshape vision model features for improved generalized category discovery by identifying low-rank compositional structures in images [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Compositional Primitive Fields (CPF-GCD), a new framework designed to improve Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) by reshaping vision model features to reveal low-rank compositional structures in images. This approach addresses the limitations of current vision backbones, which produce high-rank, entangled representations that hinder the unsupervised discovery of latent concepts. CPF-GCD models images as compositions of a finite set of learnable visual primitives arranged spatially, enabling the identification of both known and novel categories through structured, reusable components. CPF-GCD operates by inserting a spatial field mechanism between the backbone and classification head, rewriting noisy patch tokens into mixtures of low-rank primitives that capture atomic parts and their layouts. This explicit modeling of spatial distributions allows novel categories to emerge naturally as new activation patterns over a shared vocabulary. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CPF-GCD can be integrated as a plug-and-play module to consistently enhance performance across various GCD baselines, highlighting the importance of leveraging low-rank compositional structures for open-world recognition tasks.

items.title: Researchers present a Natural Semantic Metalanguage-based interface for event-based emotion analysis with causal faithfulness and release EmoExpl-1200 dataset and rule set [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed an interface for event-based emotion analysis that uses the Natural Semantic Metalanguage (NSM) framework to provide explanations that are causally and definitionally faithful to the emotion classification process. Their approach involves a parser that converts input text into a structured explication using a fixed vocabulary and a decision list of rules derived from semantic definitions, ensuring that the emotion label is computed transparently from the explication rather than through a black-box model. This method allows for auditability and verification of the classification process. The team fine-tuned the parser on crowd-sourced event descriptions, achieving moderate accuracy while prioritizing interpretability over raw performance. Alongside this interface, they released the EmoExpl-1200 dataset, which includes per-line verification metadata and the complete rule set, supporting further research and evaluation in explainable emotion analysis.

items.title: Researchers introduce LLVM-Bench and LLVM-Gym to benchmark and improve large language models for LLVM compiler issue resolution, achieving up to 21.99% resolution rate with LLVM-Ens ensemble approach [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced LLVM-Bench, the first large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on issue resolution within the LLVM compiler infrastructure, which is known for its complexity and scale. Alongside LLVM-Bench, they developed LLVM-Gym, an automated platform that facilitates issue reproduction, patch application, compiler building, and testing. Their study assessed multiple LLMs and configurations, revealing that current LLM-based methods face challenges such as patch invalidity and build failures when applied to LLVM issues. To address these limitations, the team proposed LLVM-Ens, a lightweight ensemble approach that combines patches generated by diverse techniques, filters out incorrect or redundant solutions, and selects the most promising fixes. This method improved the resolution rate to 21.99%, demonstrating enhanced effectiveness in resolving LLVM compiler issues and advancing the application of LLMs in complex system-level software maintenance.

items.title: Researchers publish strategic framework for designing impactful autonomous driving datasets, analyzing major datasets and introducing the KITScenes dataset family [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a strategic framework for designing impactful autonomous driving datasets, addressing a gap in existing literature that focuses more on dataset content than on strategic creation. Their approach emphasizes diagnosing whether research challenges stem from data or evaluation issues and selecting minimal data operations to efficiently close these gaps, recording new data only when necessary. This framework is illustrated through an analysis of major autonomous driving datasets and a case study of the newly introduced KITScenes dataset family. The framework covers key aspects such as identifying research gaps, choosing appropriate data operators, designing sensor suites, and developing annotation strategies. By applying this method, the researchers aim to help smaller labs and startups optimize resource use and avoid costly missteps in dataset creation. The KITScenes datasets are publicly available for further research and development in autonomous driving.

items.title: Researchers propose fixed-point flows to enhance self-conditioned flow map language models, improving one- and few-step text generation performance on OpenWebText [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced fixed-point flows to improve self-conditioned flow map language models, enhancing their ability to generate text in one or few steps. This approach interprets self-conditioning as a fixed-point iteration that refines the model's denoising capability, leading to a new class of models called fixed-point flows that combine the flow process with fixed-point iteration. Their model, FMLM$^\star$, demonstrates superior performance on the OpenWebText dataset compared to existing self-conditioned and few-step models. The study also presents methods to distill these fixed-point flows by compressing both the fixed-point iterations and the flow process, making the models more efficient without sacrificing accuracy. This work clarifies the theoretical underpinnings of self-conditioning in flow-based language models and offers practical advancements for text generation tasks. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration and development.

items.title: Researchers introduce PartialVisGraph, a hypergraph framework for robust skeleton-based action recognition under constrained field-of-view, achieving up to 68.8% accuracy gains on NTU RGB+D benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed PartialVisGraph, a novel hypergraph-based framework designed to improve skeleton-based action recognition in scenarios with limited field-of-view (FoV), where joint visibility is often incomplete. This approach introduces learnable virtual hyperedges and a Single-Head Sample-Adaptive Transformer that incorporates a visibility prior to prevent occluded joints from degrading feature propagation. PartialVisGraph demonstrates significant accuracy improvements, achieving up to 68.8% gains on NTU RGB+D benchmarks under severe FoV constraints compared to existing methods. The framework addresses challenges common in real-world applications such as egocentric vision, crowded surveillance, and wearable devices, where partial visibility of skeletal joints can severely impact recognition performance. By constructing expressive hypergraphs and selectively gating information flow based on joint visibility, the method maintains robust action recognition even with substantial joint dropout. Extensive evaluations on NTU RGB+D 60 and 120 datasets validate its effectiveness, showing consistent state-of-the-art results both under partial and full visibility conditions. This advancement offers a practical solution for deploying skeleton-based action recognition systems in unconstrained environments, enhancing their reliability and applicability in diverse real-world settings where sensor viewpoints are limited or obstructed.

items.title: Researchers propose ConRTF, a real-time Transformer-based table structure recognition method using edge-constrained boundary refinement and fine-grained localization loss, improving accuracy on PubTables-1M with minimal training data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed ConRTF, a real-time Transformer-based method for table structure recognition that improves the accuracy of identifying row and column layouts in document images. This approach introduces an Edge-constrained Fine-grained Localization loss (EFL) that accounts for the distinct structural roles of rows and columns by emphasizing their respective boundary orientations during training. ConRTF integrates this loss with a distribution-based boundary refinement technique, enhancing boundary precision without altering the inference process. The method demonstrates data efficiency, maintaining strong performance with as few as 2,000 to 3,000 annotated tables. Evaluations on the PubTables-1M dataset and two private datasets show that ConRTF consistently outperforms optimized baselines and several real-time detectors, including RT-DETRv2 and YOLOv10-11, achieving up to a 1.6-point improvement in GriTS score at comparable inference speeds.

items.title: Researchers find hallucinated citations in peer-reviewed papers at ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS, and USENIX Security, with about 5% of 2025 NeurIPS and USENIX papers containing multiple likely fake references [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified the presence of hallucinated citations-references to non-existent or mismatched scholarly works-in peer-reviewed papers from major conferences such as ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS, and USENIX Security. Using a tool called RefChecker, which verifies bibliography entries against multiple sources, they found that about 5% of papers at NeurIPS and USENIX Security in 2025 contained at least two likely fake references. This issue has increased following the rise of AI language models like ChatGPT, with some papers even containing five or more such citations, including award-winning works. The study highlights that while the overall rate of hallucinated citations is below 1% at the reference level, the scale of these conferences means that paper-level failures are significant. The researchers emphasize that peer review alone does not reliably prevent citation errors, but automated auditing using tools like RefChecker is feasible and cost-effective. They have made RefChecker open-source to support routine citation verification before publication, aiming to improve the integrity of scientific literature.

items.title: Researchers propose a training-free prototype memory framework for multi-class prenatal ultrasound anomaly classification and localization, validated on 1,149 cases across nine categories [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a training-free framework for classifying and localizing multiple prenatal ultrasound anomalies using only a few reference images per category. This approach addresses challenges in prenatal screening, such as the rarity and variability of anomalies and the difficulty of obtaining large annotated datasets. The framework includes a memory bank with multi-granular prototypes, a prototype-driven feature merging mechanism for anomaly detection, and a class-aware refinement strategy to enhance category prediction. The method was extensively tested on a multi-center dataset comprising 1,149 cases and 2,357 images across nine anomaly categories, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing techniques. This training-free approach offers a practical solution for resource-limited clinical settings by eliminating the need for fine-tuning on new categories, potentially improving prenatal anomaly diagnosis and management.

items.title: Researchers propose GaussianFusion, a unified 3D Gaussian representation for multi-modal fusion perception that outperforms BEVFusion on nuScenes and speeds up 3D semantic occupancy tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced GaussianFusion, a novel framework for multi-modal fusion perception that uses a unified 3D Gaussian representation instead of the traditional bird's-eye view (BEV) grid. This continuous Gaussian space preserves fine details and improves feature alignment across modalities, enhancing 3D perception tasks. GaussianFusion includes a forward-projection-based initialization and a cross-modal Gaussian encoder that updates features through attention mechanisms, making it adaptable to various 3D perception challenges. Tests on the nuScenes dataset show that GaussianFusion outperforms the BEVFusion baseline in 3D object detection by 2.6 NDS. Additionally, a variant of the model achieves a 1.55 mIoU improvement over GaussFormer in 3D semantic occupancy tasks while using only 30% of the Gaussians and running 4.5 times faster, demonstrating both efficiency and robustness.

items.title: Researchers adapt Uncertainty Herding active learning to cascaded table extraction pipelines, proposing RankFusion and CAPA extensions that improve annotation efficiency across multiple datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have adapted the Uncertainty Herding active learning method to improve annotation efficiency in cascaded table extraction pipelines, which involve Table Detection (TD) and Table Structure Recognition (TSR). They introduced two pipeline-aware extensions, RankFusion and CAPA, that leverage the dependency between TD and TSR to better balance coverage and uncertainty during sample selection.
